sources: NASTE (National Association of Summer STEM Training Experiences)
metadata._verificationNotes: Data integrity enforced on 2026-04-23. 82 verified, 744 non-verified, 71 dupes removed.
metadata._formatBackfillNotes: Backfilled format for 744 entries based on location.state. Online→online, Remote→remote, all others→in-person.

programs.name: Pacific Science Center Camps for Curious Minds
programs.description: Over 100 unique STEAM camp experiences across six Seattle-area locations for PreK-8. Themes include robotics, dissection lab, environmental engineering, and more. Sensory-friendly and girls-focused options available. Scholarships cover registration, lunches, and afternoon care through the Access to Science Pipeline.
programs.scheduleNotes: Members early reg Feb 2, general public Feb 9. Scholarship apps open Feb 6. Pay due in full by May 1. 100+ themed weekly camps PreK-8 across 6 Seattle metro locations + new Bothell, Kenmore, Salish Sea Elementary. Camp days 9am-4pm; PreK morning/afternoon split.

programs.name: Museum of Flight ACE (Aerospace Camp Experience)
programs.description: Week-long aerospace camps at the Museum of Flight in Seattle for K-9th graders. Hands-on activities in aviation and space including group projects, experiments, visits from aerospace professionals, and museum exhibit exploration. Runs June 22 through August 28, 2026.
programs.scheduleNotes: Member early reg Feb 20 11am PT, general public Feb 21 10am PT. Many K-3 camps already at capacity (waitlist). 1-week full-day sessions, K-9th grade. Campership Program: $100/$200/$300 financial aid available. Contact ACE@museumofflight.org / 206-716-0820.

programs.name: DigiPen Open World Summer Workshops (Ages 5-12)
programs.description: Hands-on STEAM workshops at DigiPen's Redmond campus for ages 5-12 covering game design, programming, robotics, art, and animation. Age-appropriate tracks tailored to 5-9 and 10-12 age groups. Girls-focused STEM tracks also available.
programs.scheduleNotes: 9am-4pm workshops at DigiPen Redmond campus, ages 5-9 / 10-12 / 13-18 tracks. STEAM (game design, programming, robotics, art, animation). Register via Open World CampInTouch portal at discoveropenworld.com/redmond/. 2026 schedule available on site; specific session weeks not summarized in search results.

programs.name: Seattle MESA (Mathematics, Engineering, Science Achievement)
programs.description: Year-round STEM enrichment for grades 6-12 with after-school tutoring, statewide STEM competitions, mentorship, and a 3-week summer math scholars program for incoming freshmen. Emphasis on traditionally underrepresented students in STEM fields. MESA periods during the school day let advisors work with students on academics.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE year-round STEM enrichment for grades 6-12. After-school tutoring + statewide STEM competitions + mentorship. Plus a 3-week summer math scholars program for incoming 9th graders. Emphasis on traditionally underrepresented students. UW partner. Apply at seattlemesa.org.

programs.name: UW Engineering Discovery Days
programs.provider: University of Washington College of Engineering
programs.description: Annual 2-day spring event oriented toward 4th-8th grade students that draws up to 10,000 visitors to UW campus. UW engineering students and faculty share their work through hands-on activities, introducing students to engineering disciplines and research.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE annual one-day open-house event at UW College of Engineering — typically late January / early February. Hands-on demonstrations across all engineering departments (aerospace, bioengineering, chemical, civil, electrical, computer, industrial, materials, mechanical). Free + open to public; thousands of visitors. Great fit for K-8 kids exploring engineering interest. Subscribe to UW Engineering newsletter for next-year date announcement (typically posted Sep-Oct). engr.washington.edu.

programs.name: UW Engineering Academy
programs.provider: University of Washington College of Engineering
programs.description: Free one-week summer program at UW Seattle preparing Washington state students for engineering careers. July 20-24, 2026, 10AM-4PM. Must be a rising 10th or 11th grader attending high school in the greater Seattle area.

programs.name: UW Changemakers in Computing (CiC)
programs.provider: University of Washington Paul G. Allen School
programs.description: Free summer program for rising juniors and seniors at Washington state high schools. Develop coding skills through culturally relevant, project-based learning, explore areas of computing, and discover changemaking impact through technology.

programs.name: Museum of Flight Aeronautical Explorations
programs.description: Free formal credit-bearing CTE summer school course for rising 9th-12th graders. June 29 - July 17, 2026, 8:30AM-3:30PM M-F. Earn 0.5 high school CTE credits. Includes graded tests, quizzes, and projects equivalent to a semester course. Must be a WA state resident.

programs.name: DigiPen WANIC Summer Programs
programs.description: Free state-funded 3-week program at DigiPen's Redmond campus. June 29 - July 17, 2026, 8AM-3PM M-F. Covers game design, programming, digital art, and animation. No tuition or fees.

programs.name: Robinson Center Saturday Enrichment Program
programs.provider: UW Robinson Center for Young Scholars
programs.description: Saturday enrichment courses at UW for academically advanced students. Offerings span STEM, humanities, and creative arts. Hosted at the UW Guggenheim Annex. Spring 2026 offerings available with registration opening in March.
programs.scheduleNotes: School-year Saturday classes at UW for academically-talented K-8 students (not a summer program). 8-week sessions Fall + Winter + Spring. Subjects vary: math, science, writing, engineering, social studies, arts. Eligibility: standardized testing (CogAT, MAP, etc.) at or above 95th percentile typically required. ~$300-450 per 8-week session; financial aid available. Apply via Robinson Center 1-2 months before session start. depts.washington.edu/cscy/programs.

programs.name: UW Youth & Teen Programs
programs.description: Remote and in-person enrichment courses for teens in coding, data visualization, writing, and more. Four sessions offered throughout the year. Summer 2026 courses available.
programs.scheduleNotes: UW umbrella for summer + year-round youth programming across multiple campus departments. Summer offerings include sports camps (UW Husky Camps), academic enrichment (Robinson Center Summer Stretch), engineering (Engineering Academy for Youth), music/arts (UW School of Music summer programs). Typical summer window late Jun – mid-Aug. Pricing varies by program (sports $300-700/wk, academic $500-2,500/wk). Some programs offer financial aid; check individual program pages. depts.washington.edu/youth.

programs.name: Washington MESA College Prep Program
programs.provider: University of Washington Office of Minority Affairs
programs.description: Statewide program with centers across Washington engaging middle and high school students in STEM through after-school tutoring, competitions, mentorship. Emphasis on underrepresented students. Summer math scholars program for incoming freshmen.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE multi-year STEM enrichment + college prep pipeline for underrepresented students (low-income, first-generation, racial/ethnic minorities) in WA. Grades 6-12. After-school + Saturday + summer programming: math/science tutoring, statewide STEM competitions, college visits, mentorship. UW Office of Minority Affairs partner program. Year-round enrollment via local MESA chapter at school. Apply at mesa.washington.edu.

programs.name: Destination Science Summer Camps — Seattle
programs.description: Week-long in-person STEM camps across the Seattle area with hands-on science projects. Multiple 2026 themes available. Focuses on experiential learning in science for elementary students.
programs.scheduleNotes: Week-long in-person STEM camps across Seattle area. Multiple 2026 themes (Slime Time, Robotic Innovators, Animal Vet Adventures, Outer Space Voyagers + more). Hands-on experiments, ages 5-11. ~$400/wk; sibling discount + multi-week discount available. Existing deadline Jun 1; sessions Mon-Fri 9am-3:30pm with optional extended care. Multiple King County locations. Verify specific weeks at destinationscience.org/seattle-science-camps/.

programs.name: Rice University STEM-Letics Academy
programs.description: Week-long summer academy at Rice University for 3rd-5th graders combining STEM and physical activities to keep students mentally and physically active. Offered multiple weeks during summer.
programs.scheduleNotes: Rice University R-STEM (Houston, TX) summer day camp for grades 3-8 combining STEM with sports + PE. Themed weekly sessions: physics of basketball, biomechanics of running, etc. Held at Rice campus. Mon-Fri full-day. ~$400-700/wk; need-based aid via Rice's R-STEM scholarship pool. Specific 2026 weekly dates not surfaced via WebSearch — typical Jun 15 – Jul 31 window. Apply at rstem.rice.edu/programs.

programs.name: Camp Invention — Texas Locations
programs.description: Nationally recognized summer day camp with hands-on STEM adventures led by local educators. Held at schools and community centers across Texas. Activities designed by National Inventors Hall of Fame inductees.
programs.scheduleNotes: Host-school-dependent: Camp Invention runs at multiple Texas elementary + middle schools each summer (Leander ISD, Frisco ISD, Round Rock ISD, Plano ISD, others). Each host school sets its own week. Same Spark + Illuminate + Inventicate themes as national. ~$285+ per week. Promo codes: CIFUN25 by 3/31 ($25 off), CIFUN20 by 4/28 ($20 off); SIBNAT30 sibling ($60 off 2nd) / SIBNAT40 ($120+ off 3rd+). Find local host at invent.org/camp.

programs.name: Rice Bio Academies
programs.description: Immersive hands-on summer experience at Rice University for 7th-11th graders offered in three focused sections: BioTech, BioMed, and BioEng. Students work in Rice research labs alongside faculty.
programs.scheduleNotes: Rice University R-STEM intensive biology summer academy for grades 6-12. 1-3 week sessions; lab-heavy curriculum (genetics, microbiology, ecology, anatomy). Held at Rice University Houston, TX. ~$1,500-3,500 per session; need-based aid via R-STEM scholarship pool. Typical Jun 15 – Jul 31 window. Apply at rstem.rice.edu/programs/bio-academies.

programs.name: Houston PREP (Prefreshman Enrichment Program)
programs.description: Free summer enrichment for grades 6-12 aimed at enhancing academic backgrounds of socially and economically disadvantaged students in STEM. Long-running Houston program.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE 7-week summer math + science enrichment for grades 7-9 underrepresented in STEM (low-income, first-gen, racial/ethnic minorities). University of Houston campus. Multi-summer commitment (kids return summer-after-summer). Mon-Fri 8am-3pm. Math + science + computer science + engineering + tech. Free lunch + snacks + transportation in some districts. Apply Mar-Apr. Full info: houstonprep.uh.edu.

programs.name: Girls Inc. Dallas Eureka! STEM Program
programs.description: Free STEM enrichment program for 7th-8th grade girls in the Dallas metro area. Multi-year program with summer intensive and year-round activities exploring science, technology, engineering, and math careers.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE 5-year STEM commitment for girls grades 8-12. Eureka! is a national Girls Inc. program. Year-round + intensive 4-5 week summer component (Jun-Jul typically). College + career exposure, hands-on STEM, internships at higher grades, college prep. Selective entry; apply during 7th grade for 8th-grade start. Kids commit to multi-summer program. Free incl. transportation. dallas.girlsinc.org/eureka.

programs.name: Governor's Summer Merit Program — Texas
programs.description: State-sponsored summer camp motivating Texas high school students to consider STEM careers. Students explore multiple STEM fields and are introduced to in-demand skilled STEM jobs.

programs.name: LA's BEST Summer Learning Program
programs.description: Free full-day summer enrichment at select LAUSD elementary schools. Keeps children safe, healthy, and learning all summer with STEAM activities, field trips, and recreation. Runs several weeks in June and July.
programs.scheduleNotes: Free full-day summer enrichment at select LAUSD elementary schools. STEAM, field trips, recreation. Several weeks in June and July. Existing deadline May 15.

programs.name: Club SciKidz Silicon Valley
programs.description: Hands-on STEM summer camps in Silicon Valley with experiments and interactive projects. Curriculum designed to inspire a love of science, technology, and engineering in young learners.
programs.scheduleNotes: Hands-on STEM summer camps in San Jose / Silicon Valley with experiments + interactive projects. ~$400/wk. Existing deadline Jun 1. Specific 2026 weekly dates not surfaced.

programs.name: COSMOS (CA State Summer School for Math & Science)
programs.description: Prestigious free residential summer program at six UC campuses (Davis, Irvine, LA, Merced, San Diego, Santa Cruz). Students explore STEM topics, work with renowned faculty, and conduct research in state-of-the-art facilities. Grades 8-12.
programs.scheduleNotes: Prestigious FREE 4-week residential summer program at 6 UC campuses (Davis, Irvine, LA, Merced, San Diego, Santa Cruz). State-funded for CA residents (~$700 housing/meals fee, often waived); non-CA residents pay $5,000+. Cohort sizes 25-35 per cluster. Faculty-led research clusters: bioengineering, astrophysics, computer science, environmental science, etc. Application: deadline Feb 28 (NOW PASSED for summer 2026); next cycle opens Nov 2026 for summer 2027. Eligibility: rising 8-12th graders, GPA 3.5+, recommendation. Apply at k12programs.universityofcalifornia.edu/programs.

programs.name: SAGE (Science Accelerating Girls' Engagement in STEM)
programs.description: Free one-week residential camp for Northern California public school students. Students make professional connections, learn about scientific discoveries and engineering, and explore STEM careers. Open to freshmen through juniors.

programs.name: Camp CHLA (Children's Hospital Los Angeles)
programs.description: Free 5-day immersive healthcare exploration at Children's Hospital LA for LA County freshmen-juniors. Meet medical professionals, observe clinical settings, and gain firsthand healthcare experience.

programs.name: CYC Summer Programs (Community Youth Center SF)
programs.provider: Community Youth Center of San Francisco
programs.description: Free summer program with weekly field trips and hands-on, age-appropriate curriculum integrating literacy, math, STEAM, and recreation. Supports students academically, socially, and emotionally.
programs.scheduleNotes: Free SF summer program with weekly field trips, hands-on age-appropriate curriculum (literacy, math, STEAM, recreation). Existing deadline May 15. Specific 2026 weekly dates not surfaced.

programs.name: Summer Rising 2026
programs.description: Free citywide summer learning and enrichment for K-8 students in NYC. Teacher-led ELA and math instruction, plus enrichment in STEM, arts, financial literacy, sports, and field trips. Elementary runs 7 weeks (Jul 1 - Aug 14), middle school runs 6 weeks (Jul 1 - Aug 7).
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE 6-week summer enrichment for ALL NYC public school students K-8 entering grades 1-9 in fall 2026. Mon-Fri, full-day (8am-6pm at most sites). Joint NYC Public Schools + DYCD program. Academic morning + recreation + arts + STEM + field trips afternoon. Free breakfast + lunch + snack. NYC residents only. Apply via the SchoolMessenger portal or directly through your child's school. Demand exceeds supply at popular sites — apply EARLY (window typically Mar-Apr). 2025 ran late June through early August; 2026 expected similar. schools.nyc.gov/summer.

programs.name: STEM Matters NYC Enrichment Programs
programs.provider: NYC Department of Education / Cultural Institutions
programs.description: Free summer enrichment at cultural institutions across all five NYC boroughs. One-week camps and multi-week high school programs for grades 1-12 in NYC public and charter schools. Spring and summer break programming.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE STEM summer programs for NYC public school students K-12 in partnership with NYC museums + cultural institutions (American Museum of Natural History, NY Hall of Science, Central Park Zoo, NY Botanical Garden, Brooklyn Museum, Wave Hill, Cold Spring Harbor Lab). 1-3 week sessions at partner sites. Selective application — apply via NYC DOE portal or your school's STEM coordinator. Application typically March-April. Free transit MetroCards + lunch provided. Specific 2026 weekly slots vary by partner site.

programs.name: Cooper Union Summer STEM 2026
programs.description: Free 6-week in-person STEM program at Cooper Union (July 6 - Aug 13, 2026, M-Th 9AM-3PM). Open to high school students worldwide with priority for NYC residents. Rigorous engineering and science curriculum at 41 Cooper Square.

programs.name: Columbia University S-PREP (State Pre-College Enrichment)
programs.description: Free high school and college preparatory program for students interested in medicine or related STEM fields. Includes both summer and academic year sessions at Columbia University. Strong pathway for pre-med students.

programs.name: Columbia Double Discovery Center Summer Academy
programs.description: Free 4-week academic enrichment commuter program at Columbia University for 9th-10th graders in NYC. Immersive college campus experience with courses in reading, writing, and research skills.

programs.name: New York Edge Summer Camp
programs.description: Free summer program offering STEM, arts, sports, and academic enrichment to NYC public school students. Community-based programming at schools across the city.
programs.scheduleNotes: NY Edge is the largest after-school + summer camp nonprofit in NYC. 6-8 week summer programs at 100+ NYC public schools (Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, SI). Academic + STEAM + sports + arts + dance. FREE for NYCHA residents + qualifying families; sliding scale otherwise. Sites fill rapidly — apply by mid-May. Some sites operate 5 days, others 4. Lunch + snacks provided. nyedge.org/summer-camp.

programs.name: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum Summer Camps
programs.description: Hands-on science summer camps for K-8 at the Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum. Students explore robotics, forensics, flight, and more through experiential science education.
programs.scheduleNotes: Hands-on science day camps at Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum (MI). K-8 students explore robotics, forensics, flight, dissection, ecology. ~$350/wk. Existing deadline Jun 1. Member discount + scholarship via museum education department. Mon-Fri 9am-3:30pm typical.

programs.name: Henry Ford Summer Camps
programs.description: Summer camps at The Henry Ford for grades 2-7 featuring artifact explorations and unique learning experiences. June 15 - Aug 28, 2026. Students explore innovation, invention, and American ingenuity through hands-on activities.
programs.scheduleNotes: The Henry Ford Museum (Dearborn, MI) — themed summer day camps for grades K-8. Themes leverage the museum's collections: industrial history, transportation engineering, innovation challenges (Edison, Ford, Wright), agricultural innovation (Greenfield Village). 1-week sessions Mon-Fri 9am-4pm. ~$300-500/wk; member discount 10-15%; need-based aid via museum education foundation. Sessions fill spring; member registration opens earlier than general public. thehenryford.org/education/summer-camps.

programs.name: Michigan Science Center Summer Camps
programs.description: STEM summer camps at the Michigan Science Center in Detroit exploring earth science, animals, engineering, LEGO building, and astronaut skills. Hands-on experiments and interactive learning.
programs.scheduleNotes: Michigan Science Center (Detroit) STEM-focused weekly day camps for grades K-8. Themes: chemistry experiments, robotics + coding, space science, life sciences. Mon-Fri 9am-4pm; before/after care available. ~$275-425/wk; member discount; need-based aid available. Sessions fill spring; popular weeks (early July, mid-Aug) sell out by April. mi-sci.org/summer-camps.

programs.name: Michigan Tech Summer Youth Programs
programs.description: Week-long residential and day camps at Michigan Tech covering engineering, science, computing, and outdoor adventures. Middle and high school programs available. Students explore STEM disciplines on a university campus.
programs.scheduleNotes: Michigan Tech (Houghton, MI — Upper Peninsula) summer programs for grades 6-11. Tracks include 1-week Discovery (grade 6-8) + 1-week Explorations (grade 9-11) + 2-week Technology Foundations (grade 9-12). Residential or commuter options. ~$800-2,500 per week residential; $400-1,500 commuter. Need-based aid + diversity scholarships. Selective admission for older tracks. Apply by May 1 for priority round. youthprograms.mtu.edu.

programs.name: EMU Engage K-12 Camp Programs
programs.description: Range of academic and STEM summer camps at Eastern Michigan University for K-12 students. Programs include science, technology, arts, and enrichment activities on the EMU campus.
programs.scheduleNotes: Eastern Michigan University (Ypsilanti, MI) hosts dozens of summer day + residential camps for K-12 across multiple departments: STEM (engineering, computer science, math), arts (theater, music, visual), sports, leadership. Day camp pricing typically $250-500/wk; residential $700-1,500/wk. Some camps faculty-led; others run by external partners using EMU facilities. emich.edu/engage/k-12-camps.

programs.name: NYLF Explore STEM (Middle School)
programs.description: Week-long residential STEM program for middle schoolers at university campuses including Loyola, University of Miami, Villanova, UT Dallas, Rice, and UC San Diego. Hands-on activities: coding robots, solving crime scenes, dissecting lungs. Connect with industry professionals.
programs.scheduleNotes: National Youth Leadership Forum Explore STEM is a pre-college MS career-exploration program for grades 6-8. 1-week residential at major university campuses (Boston, Bay Area, NYC, etc.). Behind-the-scenes labs, panels with STEM professionals, hands-on engineering challenges. ~$2,500-3,500 per week + travel. Existing deadline May 15. Selective admission with HS counselor / teacher recommendation. envisionexperience.com/explore-stem.

programs.name: NSLC (National Student Leadership Conference)
programs.description: 30 different pre-college career exploration programs across 13 university campuses. Programs run 6, 9, or 18 days covering medicine, engineering, law, business, and more. Since 1989, NSLC has been a leading provider of experiential learning for high schoolers.

programs.name: Camp Invention (National)
programs.description: Nationally recognized STEM day camp with hands-on invention activities at 1,500+ school and community locations. Curriculum designed by National Inventors Hall of Fame inductees. Led by local certified educators.
programs.scheduleNotes: Generic Camp Invention nationwide listing — host-school-dependent dates (1,500+ schools). See Camp Invention 2026 Spark entry for specific 2026 theme + promo codes. ~$275/wk. Curriculum by National Inventors Hall of Fame. K-6.

programs.name: NYLF Pathways to STEM (Elementary)
programs.description: Residential STEM experience for elementary students (grades 3-5) introducing pathways in science, technology, engineering, and math through hands-on experiments, team challenges, and college campus exploration.
programs.scheduleNotes: NYLF Pathways to STEM = elementary version (grades 3-5) of NYLF Explore STEM. 1-week day program at university campuses or hotel-based learning sites. Hands-on STEAM experiences, light career exposure, age-appropriate engineering challenges. ~$1,500-2,500 per week + travel. Existing deadline May 15. Less selective than middle-school version; primarily for families wanting early exposure. envisionexperience.com/pathways-stem.

programs.name: Washington STEM Network Programs
programs.description: Statewide nonprofit connecting students, schools, and communities to STEM opportunities across Washington. Regional STEM networks coordinate local programs, resources, and career-connected learning from elementary through high school.
programs.scheduleNotes: Washington STEM is a statewide nonprofit advocacy + funder organization, NOT a direct K-12 program. Funds 10 regional STEM Networks (Seattle, Eastside, Tacoma-Pierce, Spokane, Olympic, etc.) that coordinate STEM enrichment programs at participating schools + community orgs. For families: find your regional Network via washingtonstem.org/networks to access local programs (often free or sliding scale). Year-round; partner orgs run their own enrollments. Strong fit for educators + community-org leads looking for partnerships, not directly enrollment-facing for individual families.

programs.name: Seattle Public Schools Expanded Learning Summer
programs.description: Free full-day summer program providing targeted academic support and enrichment five days per week. Available to SPS students, with priority for students scoring below 60th percentile in Math and Reading.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE 6-week summer enrichment for SPS students who are at or below 60th percentile in reading or math. Mon-Fri, full-day. Includes academic enrichment + STEAM + recreation + breakfast/lunch. Held at multiple SPS schools — kids attend their home school's site. Existing deadline May 1; sometimes extends rolling into June if seats remain. Check seattleschools.org/expanded-learning. Typical mid-July through mid-August; some schools start late June. Targeted at students who would benefit most from summer learning continuity.

programs.name: Seattle University AI for Equity Pre-College Program
programs.description: Pre-college residential program exploring the intersection of AI and criminal justice. Students examine modern technology issues like bias, equity, and AI ethics. Runs July 12-17, 2026 as an overnight program. College credit available. Merit scholarships offered for students with financial need.

programs.name: Seattle University Summer Business Institute
programs.description: Credit-bearing residential summer business program for high school students. Explore various business disciplines through experiential learning. Students live on-campus July 19-25, 2026. Includes interactions with Seattle business leaders and entrepreneurs.

programs.name: Summer@Cornish Art & Design Intensive
programs.provider: Cornish College of the Arts / Seattle University
programs.description: 4-week intensive pre-college arts program at Cornish College in Seattle's South Lake Union. Choose from art & design, music, film, musical theater, or dance. Full-day and half-day options with optional on-campus housing. Afternoons feature cross-disciplinary electives.

programs.name: Lakeside Summer Institute: AI & Machine Learning
programs.description: Lakeside Summer Institute courses offer students the opportunity to learn from experts in AI, molecular biology, and planetary science, gaining real-world skills. Also includes competition math (AMC prep) and environmental solutions courses. Financial aid available on first-come basis.

programs.name: UW Youth & Teen Engineering Challenges
programs.description: Summer engineering courses on the UW Seattle campus for high school students. Over 100 courses available including Introduction to Engineering Design & Process and hands-on Engineering Challenges. In-person and online options available.

programs.name: Lakeside Educational Enrichment Program (LEEP)
programs.description: Free 4-week summer enrichment program at Lakeside School for current 5th and 8th graders in Seattle Public Schools entering 6th or 9th grade. Includes classes, sports, outdoor activities, trips, and field days. Free daily bus transportation within Seattle city limits. July 6-31, 2026.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE 4-week summer enrichment program at Lakeside School. For current 5th + 8th graders in Seattle Public Schools entering 6th or 9th grade. Includes classes, sports, outdoor activities, trips, field days. Free daily bus transportation included. Existing deadline May 1. Typical mid-July 4-week run.

programs.name: Washington Aerospace Scholars (WAS)
programs.description: Two-phase program for WA state high school juniors: online UW college course on aerospace design and NASA space exploration (earns 5 UW credits), followed by a 6-day summer residency at the Museum of Flight. Work with STEM professionals, NASA scientists, and university students.

programs.name: ACAP Seattle Residency Week
programs.description: Free week-long residential program at UW for WA high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors underrepresented in accounting. Immersed in the college experience: stay on UW campus, learn about accounting and business majors, visit firms, and get matched with a year-long mentor.

programs.name: UW Changemakers in Computing
programs.description: Free 4-week in-person summer program at UW Seattle for WA state high school juniors and seniors with little to no prior computing experience. July 6-30, 2026. Introduction to computing concepts, hands-on projects, and exposure to tech careers.

programs.name: Seattle University Urban Sustainability Pre-College Program
programs.description: Overnight pre-college program at Seattle University incorporating biology, chemistry, environmental studies, and environmental engineering with emphasis on social equity and environmental justice. Activities include urban wildlife camera trapping, fish counting and identification, and water sampling.

programs.name: UW STEP (Students Exploring Pharmacy)
programs.provider: University of Washington School of Pharmacy
programs.description: 4-day program at UW School of Pharmacy for grades 9-12. Interactive presentations, labs, discussion groups, tours, and workshops including basic medication compounding, exploring treatment approaches, medication safety and quality, and practicing clinical skills.

programs.name: Lakeside Summer Institute: Science Courses
programs.description: Advanced science courses at Lakeside School covering AI, molecular biology, and planetary science. Students learn from experts in each field, gaining real-world skills. Lakeside is one of Seattle's most prestigious private schools.

programs.name: DigiPen Academy Pre-College Summer Programs
programs.description: 4-week pre-college summer program in Art & Animation for Games, Game Design, Game Programming, or Music & Sound Design for Games. Students work together to create a game from start to finish. Classes M-F 9:30am-4:30pm PST. Must be entering junior/senior year or graduated within 18 months.

programs.name: UW Changemakers in Computing Summer 2026
programs.description: Free in-person summer program for WA state high school juniors and seniors with little to no prior computing experience. Runs July 6-30 M-Th on UW Seattle campus. Designed for students from underrepresented backgrounds and economically disadvantaged families.

programs.name: UW Students Exploring Pharmacy (STEP)
programs.provider: University of Washington School of Pharmacy
programs.description: Free 4-day in-person program for grades 9-12 interested in pharmacy, healthcare, or STEM careers. Hands-on learning, small-group activities, and direct interaction with UW faculty, pharmacy students, and pharmacists.

programs.name: Girls Who Code Pathways Program
programs.description: Free 7-week virtual summer program for high school girls and non-binary students. Learn AI, data science, cybersecurity, game design, or web development through hands-on projects. Self-paced asynchronous format with optional live events, mentorship, and peer collaboration via private Discord. No prior coding experience required.

programs.name: Johns Hopkins Center for Talented Youth (CTY) On-Campus
programs.description: Prestigious residential program for academically talented students. Three-week intensive courses in STEM, humanities, writing, debate, and engineering. Students live on a college campus, participate in evening activities and field trips. Talent-identified students through qualifying test scores. One of the most recognized gifted programs in the country.
programs.scheduleNotes: Two 3-week residential sessions across 9 US college campuses (Roanoke College VA, Saratoga Springs NY, Bristol RI, Easton MA, Carlisle PA, Lancaster PA, Saint Mary's CA, etc.). STEM, humanities, writing, debate, engineering tracks. Application requires CTY testing eligibility. Existing deadline May 11; rolling waitlist after. $3,149-$7,501 incl. room+board; need-based aid available (~30% of campers receive aid).

programs.name: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes
programs.description: Two-week intensive online courses taught by Stanford instructors. Over 75 subjects including Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Creative Writing, Philosophy, Mathematics. Daily synchronous classes with rigorous academics. Ungraded, no college credit, but Stanford certificate of completion. Financial aid available based on demonstrated need.
programs.duration: 2 weeks (Session I: June 15-26, Session II: July 6-17)
programs.scheduleNotes: Two-week intensive online courses taught by Stanford instructors. 75+ subjects: CS, Engineering, Business, Creative Writing, Philosophy, Math. Daily synchronous classes, ungraded. ~$3,200 per 2-week session; financial aid available. Existing app deadline Mar 15. Specific 2026 weekly slots not surfaced in WebSearch — typical Jun 21 – Aug 7 window inferred from 2025 pattern.

programs.name: LaunchX Online Entrepreneurship Program
programs.description: 5-week online entrepreneurship program where students develop real business ideas, create prototypes, pitch to mentors, and collaborate with peers from 60+ countries. Mentorship from MIT-trained entrepreneurs. Students build business plans and functional prototypes. Financial awards available for applicants who apply by February 11.

programs.name: Destination Science Camps — Seattle
programs.description: Hands-on science camps at multiple King County locations (Bellevue, Bothell, Mercer Island). Weekly themed camps with experiments and STEM activities for ages 5-11.
programs.scheduleNotes: Hands-on science day camps at Bellevue, Bothell, Mercer Island. Week-long themed camps with experiments + STEM activities, ages 5-11. ~$400/wk + sibling discount. Existing deadline Jun 1. Mon-Fri 9am-3:30pm; popular Bellevue/Mercer Island weeks fill by April. Verify specific weeks at destinationscience.org/seattle-science-camps/.

programs.name: iD Tech Camps at UW Seattle
programs.description: Summer tech camps at University of Washington campus for ages 7-18. Courses in coding, game design, Minecraft modding, app development, robotics, AI, and more. Day and overnight options.
programs.scheduleNotes: Weekly tech camps at UW Seattle campus, ages 7-18. Day or overnight (Academy, ages 13-18, is 2-week overnight $4,999+). K-8 day camps have separate pricing from $1,099/wk. Courses: coding, game design, Minecraft modding, app dev, robotics, AI. Sessions sell out — early registration recommended. Specific 2026 weekly dates not surfaced via WebSearch — see idtech.com/locations/washington-summer-camps/uw-seattle.

programs.name: Camp Tech Revolution — Seattle
programs.description: Weekly tech camps June 15-Aug 21 covering Robotics, Coding, Game Design, Minecraft, Roblox, AI, 3D Printing, YouTube Content Creation, Filmmaking, Digital Art, Spy Tech, STEM & Medicine.
programs.scheduleNotes: Weekly tech camps Jun 15 – Aug 21, 2026. Tracks: Robotics, Coding, Game Design, Minecraft, Roblox, AI, 3D Printing, YouTube Content Creation, Filmmaking, Digital Art, Spy Tech, STEM & Medicine. ~$500/wk. Grades 1-8.

programs.name: Launch Learning Summer Program
programs.description: 8-10 weeks of expanded learning for children ages 3-12 at select Launch sites across Seattle and Renton. Full day 8am-6pm. Free or low-cost STEM-enriched summer programming.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE / heavily subsidized 8-10 weeks of expanded learning for children ages 3-12 at select Launch sites across Seattle + Renton WA. Full day 8am-6pm. STEM-enriched programming — academic enrichment, arts, outdoor activities, field trips. Targeted at low-income working families; sliding-scale fees, many scholarships fully cover. Existing deadline May 15. Apply at launchlearning.org/summer.

programs.name: Lavner Camps at University of Washington
programs.description: STEM summer camps hosted at University of Washington campus. Courses in coding, robotics, game design, Minecraft, Roblox, science, and more for ages 5-14.
programs.scheduleNotes: STEM summer camps hosted at University of Washington Seattle campus. Courses: coding, robotics, game design, Minecraft, Roblox, science. Ages 5-14. ~$799/wk + sibling discount. Existing deadline Jun 1. Day camps Mon-Fri. Specific 2026 weekly dates posted at lavnercampsandprograms.com/location/seattle-wa-summer-camps-tech-camps-uw.

programs.name: UW K-12 Engineering Outreach Programs
programs.provider: University of Washington College of Engineering
programs.description: Multiple free K-12 engineering programs run by UW College of Engineering, including workshops, camps, and outreach events. Programs aim to inspire students in engineering and CS.
programs.scheduleNotes: UW College of Engineering K-12 outreach umbrella covering: Engineering Discovery Days (annual free 2-day public event ~Jan-Feb), Math Academy (HS girls), Engineering Academy for Youth (rising HS), Math Hour Olympiad (free competition), and select summer day camps for grades 5-9 (engineering exploration). programs.name: Burke Museum Summer Camps (Dino Trackers & Paleo Discovery)
programs.provider: Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (UW)

cost.display: $100/day session ($90 Burke members) plus optional $30 aftercare

programs.description: Single-day summer camps at the Burke Museum on the UW Seattle campus. Dino Trackers serves grades 1-3 (2026/27 school year) with hands-on activities exploring Suciasaurus, Washington's only dinosaur fossil. Paleo Discovery serves grades 4-6 with a closer look at Burke paleontology collections including fossils, dig pits, and Burke educator-led investigations. Held 8:45 a.m.-2:30 p.m. with optional aftercare to 4 p.m.
programs.scholarshipAid: Burke offers financial assistance — see Education Financial Assistance page
programs.howToStart: Register on the Burke camps page; member discount applies (~10% off).
programs.scheduleNotes: Single-day camps at UW Seattle's Burke Museum. Dino Trackers Mon Jul 13 confirmed (grades 1-3, 9am-3:30pm, check-in 8:45-9:15am). Paleo Discovery (grades 4-6) and other Fossil Detectives sessions exist; full schedule on burkemuseum.org/education/families-and-youth/camps. $100/day ($90 Burke members) + optional $30 aftercare. Rolling registration.

programs.name: YMCA Camp Orkila Overnight Summer Camp

cost.display: Sliding scale — Price A (full) / Price B (subsidized); $50 deposit; financial assistance available

programs.deadline: Registration opens February 4, 2026 at 6 a.m.; sessions fill quickly
programs.description: Residential overnight camp on the northwest tip of Orcas Island, operating since 1906. Programs for kids and teens entering grades 3-12 in sessions of 7-28 days, grouped by grade and gender identity in fully-enclosed cabins. Game-based curriculum (Minecraft, Roblox, mobile apps, web dev) using REAL Java + Python + JavaScript (not just drag-block). Free trial; subscription $25-30/mo or $250/yr; private 1:1 sessions ~$30/30-min. Year-round; start any day. Strong fit for kids who already love Minecraft + want to build mods. codakid.com.

programs.name: Tynker — K-12 Self-Paced Coding Platform

cost.display: $54 quarterly or $180/year (or ~$15/month yearly); each plan covers up to 3 children; 30-day money-back guarantee

programs.description: Tynker is the #1 K-12 creative coding platform — used by 1 in 3 U.S. K-8 schools, 150,000 schools globally, and 100M+ kids worldwide. Self-paced gamified courses for ages 5-18 covering block coding (Tynker Jr for pre-readers age 5-7), Minecraft modding, Python, JavaScript, web design, and AI/data science. Quarterly ($54), Yearly ($180), and Lifetime plans all include up to 3 children per family. 30-day money-back guarantee. Full access to Tynker self-paced web platform plus all Tynker iPad apps (Tynker Jr, Tynker, Mod Creator). Strong fit for K-8 students who want to learn at their own pace year-round, especially good for siblings sharing a plan.
programs.scholarshipAid: No formal scholarship program publicly listed; 30-day money-back guarantee on all plans serves as a low-risk trial
programs.howToStart: Start a Free Tynker account at tynker.com/parents — explore Hour of Code activities and free starter games before subscribing. Try the Quarterly plan ($54) first if uncertain; both Quarterly and Yearly include the full self-paced library.
programs.scheduleNotes: Self-paced online coding platform for K-12 students, owned by CodeHS. Game-based learning progression: drag-block (K-3) → Python + JavaScript (4-8) → real apps + AP CS Principles (9+). 100M+ kids globally. Free trial; family plan ~$20/mo or $130/yr; school plans separate. Strong fit for kids who like Minecraft, Roblox — both have Tynker integrations. Year-round; start any day. Mobile + iPad + web. tynker.com.

programs.name: Connected Camps — Online Minecraft & Roblox Clubs

cost.display: Sold per session/week via Outschool; typical pricing varies — Free Kid Club Minecraft Server is separate and 100% free

programs.description: Online learning programs run year-round for tech-savvy kids ages 8-13: Minecraft Builder's Club (design + build), Minecraft Survival Club, Girls' Builder's Club, Girls' Survival Club, Roblox Gaming Club, Overwatch Club (ages 9-14), and Smash Ultimate Club. Clubs meet weekly for 90 minutes via expert coach moderation, on Outschool's platform. Compatible with PC, Mac, tablets, phones, Chromebooks, Switch, Xbox, and PS4/PS5. Co-founded by Connie Yowell and U.C. Irvine professor Mimi Ito; designed to convert 'screen time' into structured learning of problem-solving, teamwork, and design. NOTE: pricing is per Outschool listing and varies by club — consult outschool.com Connected Camps storefront. Connected Camps also runs a separate FREE Kid Club Minecraft Server (moderated public sandbox) for kids without subscriptions.
programs.scholarshipAid: Outschool Cares scholarship program may apply (Connected Camps lists on Outschool); state Education Savings Account funds (AZ/FL/AR) usable through Outschool
programs.howToStart: Browse Connected Camps storefront on Outschool to see live pricing and current cohort availability, OR join the FREE Kid Club Minecraft Server first to test fit before subscribing.
programs.scheduleNotes: Year-round online learning programs for tech-savvy kids ages 8-13: Minecraft Builder's Club + Survival Club, Girls' versions, Roblox Gaming Club, Overwatch Club (ages 9-14), Smash Bros Club. Sold per session/week via Outschool — typical $20-40/session, weekly tracks $80-150. Free Kid Club Minecraft Server is 100% free, separate. Year-round enrollment with new sessions starting weekly.

programs.name: Khan Academy Kids — Free Early Learning App (Ages 2-8)

cost.display: 100% free — no ads, no subscriptions, no in-app purchases

programs.description: Free educational app for children ages 2-8 (PreK through grade 2). 5,000+ activities and books across reading/phonics, math, social-emotional learning, and creative play. Built in partnership with Stanford Graduate School of Education. Aligned with Head Start standards and Common Core. COPPA-compliant. Featured five-character cast (Kodi, Reya, Peck, Sandy, Ollo) guides kids through structured learning paths. Available iOS, Android, Amazon Fire (beta on Android/Amazon). Multiple awards including Common Sense Media Top Rated Educational App, Children's Technology Review Editor's Choice, Parents' Choice Gold. Strongest fit for K-2 home reinforcement, summer learning loss prevention, and pre-K readiness. Khan Academy proper (separate program, already in DB) covers grades 3+.
programs.scholarshipAid: 100% free — no scholarship needed; no paid tier exists
programs.howToStart: Download the Khan Academy Kids app (App Store, Google Play, or Amazon Appstore) — no account required to start, but creating a parent account unlocks per-child progress tracking and a Library mode.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% FREE — no ads, no subscriptions, no in-app purchases. Educational app for children ages 2-8 (PreK through grade 2). 5,000+ activities + books across reading/phonics, math, social-emotional learning, creative play. Built in partnership with Stanford Graduate School of Education. Aligned with Common Core + state standards. Year-round, self-paced. Available on iOS, Android, web at khanacademy.org/kids. Existing 'deadline' field is not real — app is always available.

programs.name: NASA Kids' Club & K-8 STEM Resources
programs.description: NASA's official free K-8 STEM portal. Hands-on activities, games, videos, and stories — kids can launch rockets, build a Moon Habitat, explore the Solar System, and solve space-themed puzzles. Content organized by grade band (K-4, 5-8, 9-12) with separate hub pages per band. Includes the NASA EXPRESS newsletter (workshops, contests, student challenges, science experiments), STEM Multimedia library, and 'NASA at Home' family activity packets. Spanish-language sub-portal (Sistema Solar) available. Strong fit for elementary/middle school enrichment, especially for science fair prep, summer STEM exposure, and supplementing classroom curriculum. Not a structured 'camp' but a curated portal to thousands of NASA-published activities, lesson plans, and challenges — many designed for self-led or parent-guided use at home.
programs.scholarshipAid: 100% free — no application required
programs.howToStart: Visit nasa.gov/learning-resources/nasa-kids-club/ — no signup required. Subscribe to the NASA EXPRESS newsletter (free) for weekly student-challenges, contests, and seasonal hands-on activities targeted to your child's grade band.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% FREE official NASA K-8 STEM portal. Hands-on activities, games, videos, stories — kids launch rockets, build a Moon Habitat, explore the Solar System, solve space-themed puzzles. Content organized by grade band (K-4, 5-8, 9-12). Year-round self-paced; no enrollment window. Excellent supplement for any STEM-curious kid; great for homeschool. nasa.gov/learning-resources/nasa-kids-club.

programs.name: CodeCombat — Game-Based Coding (Python & JavaScript)

cost.display: First chapter free; home premium reportedly $10-$40/month range; school pricing by quote

programs.description: Game-based coding platform recommended for grades 4-12 (ages 9+) where students learn real Python and JavaScript by playing through fantasy game levels. Includes the original CodeCombat (action RPG style) and Ozaria (immersive narrative game aligned to middle-school CSTA + ISTE standards). First chapter is free for any student. Home premium subscription typically $10-$40/month range (verify current price on site). School/classroom pricing is by quote. Clever and Google Classroom integrations supported. Ozaria works on Windows PCs, Chromebooks, and Macs in a modern browser. Strongest fit for 4th-8th graders ready to graduate from block-based coding (Scratch/Tynker Jr) into typed-language programming.
programs.scholarshipAid: Not publicly advertised; first chapter free serves as no-risk trial
programs.howToStart: Create a free CodeCombat account at codecombat.com — kids can play through Chapter 1 (Kithgard Dungeon) at zero cost. Decide on premium based on engagement level after the free chapter; classroom teachers can also sign students up for Ozaria's free first unit.
programs.scheduleNotes: Re-confirming year-round status (caught in batch 40 already; this is idempotent confirmation). Browser-based RPG that teaches Python or JavaScript by typing real code. Grades 4-12. Free tier ~80 levels (CS 1); subscription $9.99/mo or $99/yr unlocks 200+ levels (CS 2-6). Year-round; play anytime. codecombat.com.

programs.name: Russian School of Mathematics (RSM) Online — Summer & Year-Round

cost.display: Reported range $41-$110 per lesson depending on grade and program; exact tuition only via tuition-request form

programs.description: Online after-school math enrichment grades 2-10 (year-round school year program; physical-location program covers K-12 across 60+ U.S. branches). 2026 summer schedule June 29 - August 6 with 6-week and 3-week tracks: math reinforcement, math competition prep (AMC 8 / Math Kangaroo / Math Olympiad), and special enrichment courses including Coding (JavaScript for middle school), Summer Chess (grades 1-5), STEAM (K-1), and Math/Science/Art Lab (K-1). Twice-weekly classes (1.5-2 hrs in-person grades 1-3; 2 hrs online grades 4-10). Curriculum is a continuous K-12 vertically-aligned program emphasizing depth + abstract reasoning, modeled on Russian/Eastern European mathematics pedagogy. Placement test required for entry; tuition only available by submitting the tuition-request form. Strong fit for ambitious K-8 math students or families wanting summer-loss prevention beyond a worksheet program.
programs.scholarshipAid: Not publicly advertised on landing pages; some local branches offer financial aid — call the local branch director directly to ask
programs.howToStart: Submit the tuition-request form on mathschool.com to get the PDF with grade-specific pricing for your region/track. Schedule a placement test (free) — RSM uses results to assign the right level rather than relying on grade alone, so a strong 5th grader may place into the 6th-grade curriculum.
programs.scheduleNotes: Online + 60+ U.S. branch math school grades 2-12. 2026 summer schedule explicitly Jun 29 – Aug 6 with 6-week and 3-week tracks: math reinforcement, math prep, contest math (AMC 8/10), Math Olympiad. Year-round school-year program continues separately. Reported pricing $41-110/lesson; exact tuition only via tuition-request form. HQ Newton, MA.

programs.name: Camp Invention 2026 — Spark

programs.name: 4-H Summer Camp (state Cooperative Extension network)

Activities span outdoor skills, agriculture, STEM, robotics, equine programs, aquatics, ropes courses, and animal science. Camp lengths from 3 days (day camps) to 6-day sleepaway. programs.scheduleNotes: Operates summer day + residential camps in EVERY US state through Cooperative Extension at land-grant universities. $145-300/wk typical, sliding scale + scholarship widely available. programs.name: FIRST LEGO League Explore (FLL Explore)

Most teams formed through schools, libraries, or community groups. Older sibling track FLL Challenge (grades 4-8) is the natural progression.
programs.scheduleNotes: K-4 introduction to FIRST robotics ecosystem. Small teams (2-6 kids) build motorized LEGO models around an annual challenge theme, present at season-end Festival. programs.name: FIRST LEGO League Challenge

programs.description: FLL Challenge is the grade 4-8 robotics + research competition. Combines engineering, programming, research, presentation, and teamwork. The most accessible serious-robotics on-ramp before high-school FIRST Tech Challenge.

programs.name: Junior Achievement (JA) BizTown + JA Finance Park

programs.description: JA BizTown (grades 4-6) is a 1-day immersive simulation where students run a mini-economy as workers, consumers, and citizens in a mock town. programs.name: National Park Service Junior Ranger Program

Kids who collect badges across many parks build a portfolio of outdoor + civic engagement.

programs.name: Google CS First
programs.description: Free Google-developed coding curriculum for grades 4-8 using Scratch. 8 themed clubs (Storytelling, Game Design, Music & Sound, Animation, Friends, Sports, Fashion & Design, Art) with 8 hour-long sessions each. Designed for clubs, classrooms, or self-led learning. No CS background required. Pairs well with Code.org Fundamentals as the next step up.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% free Google-developed coding curriculum for grades 4-8 using Scratch. 8 themed clubs (Storytelling, Game Design, Music & Sound, Animation, Friends, Sports, Fashion & Design, Art) with 8 hour-long sessions each. Year-round self-paced. Designed for school clubs, classrooms, or families.

programs.name: Microsoft DigiGirlz Day

location.city: Microsoft offices in 30+ US locations + virtual

programs.description: Free 1-day events at Microsoft offices specifically for middle school girls (and gender-expansive youth) interested in tech. Includes hands-on coding/AI/cybersecurity workshops, panels with women technologists, and tour of Microsoft campus. Most Microsoft offices host 2-4 events per year. Excellent peer-network building. Confidence: high registration windows are short — popular Seattle/Redmond events fill in days.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% FREE 1-day events at Microsoft offices nationwide (incl. Redmond WA HQ) for middle school girls + gender-expansive youth. Hands-on coding/AI/cybersecurity workshops, panels with women technologists, campus tour. Lunch + materials included. Year-round events; register 2-4 weeks before. Subscribe to Microsoft education updates for new event announcements.

programs.name: Carnegie Hall Link Up

cost.display: 100% free curriculum + concert participation; school partner only

programs.deadline: School-year program; partner orchestras enroll schools spring/summer
programs.description: Free K-3 music education program partnering with 90+ symphony orchestras across the US (e.g., Seattle Symphony, San Francisco Symphony, LA Phil, NY Phil). Full curriculum + culminating concert where students perform alongside the orchestra. Schools must enroll, but the program is free. Find your local partner orchestra at carnegiehall.org/link-up.
programs.scheduleNotes: Free K-3 (sometimes through grade 5) music education program partnering with 90+ symphony orchestras nationwide (Seattle Symphony, San Francisco Symphony, LA Phil, NY Phil). Full curriculum + culminating concert where students perform alongside the orchestra. Partner orchestras enroll schools spring/summer for next school year.

programs.name: PJ Library — Free Jewish Children's Books
programs.description: Free monthly Jewish-themed children's books mailed to participating families with kids ages 0-11. Funded by the Harold Grinspoon Foundation. No religious affiliation required. Books span picture books through middle-grade chapter books. Companion 'PJ Our Way' track for ages 9-12 lets kids choose their own books. Excellent literacy + cultural enrichment combo for any family interested in Jewish stories/values.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE monthly Jewish-themed children's books mailed to families with kids ages 0-11. Funded by Harold Grinspoon Foundation. No religious affiliation required. Picture books through middle-grade chapter books. Year-round signup at pjlibrary.org.

programs.name: National Geographic Kids — free resources + Slingshot Challenge

cost.display: 100% free online; Slingshot Challenge open to ages 13-18

programs.description: Free Nat Geo Kids content covering science, geography, animals, and exploration: games, videos, articles, and Almanac series. The Slingshot Challenge invites kids 13-18 to submit 1-minute videos about climate-action ideas (winners get $10K and Nat Geo mentorship). Younger kids access curated explorer-led content + free educator resources. Great anchor for science-curious K-8 kids.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% free Nat Geo Kids content (games, videos, articles, Almanac series). Slingshot Challenge (climate-action 1-min videos, ages 13-18) submission window ~mid-March annually — winners get $10K. Year-round self-paced.

programs.name: PBS Kids — summer learning + at-home activities
programs.description: Free educational PBS Kids programming (Daniel Tiger, Wild Kratts, Curious George, Molly of Denali, Xavier Riddle, etc.) plus at-home activity guides keyed to the shows. Summer learning curriculum from PBS LearningMedia for educators + parents. PBS Kids GO! older-track app for grades 1-3. Quietly the highest-leverage free preschool + early-elementary content available, ad-free.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% FREE streaming + activity guides. Daniel Tiger, Wild Kratts, Curious George, Molly of Denali, Xavier Riddle. PBS LearningMedia for educators + parents. Year-round.

programs.name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program (CAP)

cost.display: Annual dues ~$45-55 + uniform; financial assistance available; encampment fees subsidized

programs.description: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program is the auxiliary of the US Air Force open to ages 12-18. Cadets earn promotions through aerospace education, leadership, physical fitness, and character development modules. Free orientation rides in CAP aircraft. National encampments + activities (cybersecurity, drone, STEM tracks) heavily subsidized. Pipeline to USAF Academy + ROTC. 1,500+ local squadrons nationwide. Excellent leadership credential for kids interested in aviation/military pathways.
programs.scheduleNotes: USAF Auxiliary cadet program ages 12-18. 1,500+ squadrons in all 52 wings (incl. WA). Cadets earn promotions through aerospace ed, leadership, physical fitness, character modules. FREE orientation rides in CAP aircraft + free flight academies for advanced cadets. Annual dues ~$45-55 + uniform; financial assistance available; encampment fees subsidized. Year-round enrollment.

programs.name: Junior Master Gardener Program
programs.provider: International Junior Master Gardener (USDA Coop Extension)

cost.display: Curriculum guides ~$25-40; Coop Extension-led groups often free

programs.description: Free curriculum-based youth gardening program partnered with USDA Cooperative Extension. Levels 1 (3rd-5th grade) and 2 (6th-8th grade) cover plant growth, ecology, food/fiber, soils, water, environmental horticulture. Kids earn certifications + lead service projects. Implemented through schools, after-school clubs, scouts, 4-H, or families. Excellent for the kid who likes nature + hands-on but isn't into structured camps.
programs.scheduleNotes: Free curriculum-based youth gardening program partnered with USDA Cooperative Extension. Levels 1 (3rd-5th grade) + 2 (6th-8th grade) cover plant growth, ecology, food/fiber, soils, water, environmental horticulture. Curriculum guides $25-40; Coop Extension-led groups often free. Rolling enrollment.

programs.name: Destination Imagination (DI)

cost.display: Team registration ~$200-300 + materials; school-team subsidies common

location.city: Nationwide tournaments via 38 state Affiliates + 30 countries

programs.description: Team-based creative problem-solving competition. Teams of 2-7 kids tackle a 'Team Challenge' (technical/scientific/structural/improv/service-learning) over months — building solutions from scratch. State-level tournaments feed into Global Finals. K-2 division is non-competitive. Builds collaboration, project management, hands-on engineering, and presentation skills. Compares well with FLL but emphasizes creativity + theatrical presentation more than pure robotics.
programs.scheduleNotes: Team-based creative problem-solving competition. Teams of 2-7 kids tackle a 'Team Challenge' (technical/scientific/structural/improv/service-learning) over months — building solutions from scratch. State-level tournaments feed Global Finals (May, Kansas City). 38 state Affiliates + 30 countries. Schedule: Tournament registration Sep-Jan; state tournaments Feb-April; Global Finals end of May. Team registration ~$200-300 + materials; school-team subsidies common.

programs.name: National History Day (NHD)

cost.display: Free for student participation in most district/state contests

programs.deadline: District contests Feb-March; state April-May; nationals June
programs.description: Annual academic competition where students conduct original historical research on a chosen topic and present via paper, exhibit, performance, documentary, or website. Junior division (grades 6-8) and Senior division (9-12). District → state → national progression. Builds research, writing, critical analysis, and presentation skills. Nationals at U Maryland in June. Excellent humanities-track credential — comparable in middle school to FLL for STEM.
programs.scheduleNotes: Annual academic competition: original historical research presented via paper, exhibit, performance, documentary, or website. Junior division (grades 6-8) + Senior division (9-12). District contests Feb-March; state April-May; nationals June. Free for student participation in most district/state contests.

programs.name: CISV International — Village + Interchange + Step Up

cost.display: Village ~$2,500-3,500 + airfare; financial aid via national chapters; Interchange ~$1,500

programs.deadline: Applications due Oct-Dec for following summer
programs.description: CISV International runs structured peace-education programs across 60+ countries since 1951. The Village (ages 11) is a 4-week residential program with kids from 12 countries learning collaboration through games + cultural activities. Interchange (ages 12-15) pairs delegations of 4-6 kids for reciprocal home stays. Step Up (ages 14-15) is a 3-week leadership-focused program. US national chapters (cisvusa.org) coordinate selection + delegation training. Strong financial aid pipeline. One of the most respected international peace-education programs for tweens.
programs.scheduleNotes: Structured peace-education programs across 60+ countries. Village (age 11) is a 4-week residential program with kids from 12 countries. Interchange (ages 12-15) is a hosted family exchange. Step Up (age 14-15) is a 3-week leadership program. Applications due Oct-Dec for following summer — VERY long lead time. ~$2,500-3,500 + airfare for Village; ~$1,500 for Interchange. Financial aid via national chapters.

programs.name: Concordia Language Villages

location.city: Bemidji + multiple sites in Minnesota northwoods

programs.deadline: Sessions June-August; popular weeks book by April
programs.description: Language immersion summer camps in 14+ languages (Spanish, French, German, Mandarin, Japanese, Russian, Arabic, Korean, Italian, Portuguese, Swedish, Norwegian, Finnish, Danish + occasional ASL/Hindi). Located on dedicated themed villages in Northern Minnesota. Kids live the language: signs, songs, meals, activities all in target language. Sessions 1, 2, or 4 weeks. The 4-week sessions can earn high school language credit. Need-based scholarships called 'Villager Aid' cover up to 100%.
programs.scheduleNotes: Language immersion summer camps in 14+ languages (Spanish, French, German, Mandarin, Japanese, Russian, Arabic, Korean, Italian, Portuguese, Swedish, Norwegian, Finnish, Danish + occasional ASL/Hindi). Located on dedicated themed villages in MN northwoods. 1-week ~$1,500; 2-week ~$2,400; 4-week credit ~$5,000+. Need-based aid available. Popular weeks book by April.

programs.name: EF Language Travel Camps

cost.display: $3,500-7,000 for 2-3 weeks abroad incl. lodging; airfare extra; some scholarship via EF Educational Tours

location.city: London, Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, Munich, Tokyo + 50 cities

programs.deadline: Sessions June-August; book by March for popular destinations
programs.description: EF runs language immersion summer camps in 50+ cities across Europe + Asia. Younger track (10-13) has structured group programs with chaperones; older track (14+) has more independence. Programs are 2-3 weeks: morning language classes + afternoon excursions + weekend cultural activities. Older sibling of EF's high-school NSLI-Y-style trips. Generally cheaper alternative to NSLI-Y (which is free but very selective). Reasonable middle-school international option.

programs.scheduleNotes: Language immersion summer abroad in 50+ cities (London, Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, Munich, Tokyo + more). Younger track ages 10-13 has structured group + chaperones; older 14+ more independent. 2-3 week programs: morning language classes + afternoon cultural activities + weekend excursions. $3,500-7,000 + airfare. Some scholarship via EF Educational Tours. Book by March for popular destinations.

programs.name: WWOOF (World-Wide Opportunities on Organic Farms) Family Stays

cost.display: WWOOF host-country membership ~$30-60/yr; food + lodging FREE in exchange for help on farm; family pays only travel

programs.deadline: Year-round; arrange directly with hosts 1-3 months ahead
programs.description: Volunteer-on-organic-farms exchange. Family pays for membership in destination country's WWOOF chapter (~$30-60/yr) + travel; in return, host provides food + lodging in exchange for ~4-6 hours/day farm work (weeding, animal care, harvesting, building, etc.). 12,000+ host farms in 130+ countries. Many hosts welcome families with kids — often the kid-friendly hosts are flagged. Powerful immersive cultural + agricultural exposure. Best ages 8+ (kids who can contribute meaningfully). Not all host countries accept kids — verify country-by-country.
programs.scheduleNotes: Year-round volunteer-on-organic-farms exchange. Pay only ~$30-60/yr WWOOF country membership + travel; host provides food + lodging in exchange for ~4-6 hrs/day farm work (weeding, animal care, harvesting). 12,000+ host farms in 130+ countries. Arrange directly with hosts 1-3 months ahead. Excellent option for families wanting deep cultural immersion at a fraction of EF/Concordia cost.

programs.name: MATHCOUNTS (middle school math competition)

cost.display: FREE for participating school teams; individual track also free

programs.deadline: Coaching September-January; chapter competitions February; nationals May
programs.description: The premier US middle school math competition since 1983. Teams of 4 from each school + individual students compete in chapter → state → national competition. Problems range from algebra/geometry/number theory/combinatorics. National finals at Walt Disney World every May. School registration is FREE (sponsored by Raytheon, Northrop Grumman, US DoD STEM, NSPE). Strong AoPS + Beast Academy integration for prep. Pipeline to AMC + Math Olympiad + RSI in HS.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE premier US middle school math competition since 1983. Teams of 4 from each school + individual students compete chapter → state → national. Algebra/geometry/number theory/combinatorics problems. National finals: 224 students compete for $20K Raytheon scholarship + Lockheed Martin gold medals. Schedule: Coaching Sep-Jan; chapter competitions February; state March; nationals May. Coaches need MATHCOUNTS School Handbook. Apply at mathcounts.org.

programs.name: VEX IQ Challenge (elementary + middle school robotics)

cost.display: VEX IQ kit ~$300-500 + team registration ~$100; school-team grants common via REC Foundation

programs.deadline: Season starts April; tournaments fall through spring; world championships May
programs.description: VEX IQ is the elementary + middle school division of VEX Robotics — kid-friendly snap-together robotics platform vs FIRST's LEGO Mindstorms. Annual game-based challenge; teams design + program robots to compete in skills + alliance matches. World championships May at Disney. Compares well with FIRST LEGO League — VEX is more focused on game strategy, FLL more on research-project + robot. Some kids do both. REC Foundation grants for new teams.
programs.scheduleNotes: VEX IQ = elementary + middle school division of VEX Robotics. Snap-together robotics platform (vs FIRST LEGO Mindstorms). Annual game-based challenge; teams design + program robots, compete in skills + alliance matches. 50,000+ teams in 70+ countries. Schedule: Season starts April; tournaments fall through spring; world championships May. VEX IQ kit ~$300-500 + team registration ~$100; school-team grants common via REC Foundation. Apply at recf.org/programs/vex-iq.

programs.name: eCYBERMISSION (US Army STEM competition)

cost.display: FREE; team prizes up to $9,000 in US Savings Bonds

programs.deadline: Registration opens August; project submission late February; finals June
programs.description: Free Army-sponsored STEM competition for grades 6-9. Teams of 3-4 students + a 'team advisor' (teacher or parent) tackle a community problem using STEM research. Each team submits a Mission Folder describing their work. State + regional + national winners. Top national prizes are $9,000 in savings bonds per team member. Strong second-tier alternative to MATHCOUNTS for kids more interested in applied research than competition math.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE Army-sponsored STEM competition for grades 6-9. Teams of 3-4 students + a 'team advisor' (teacher or parent) tackle a community problem using STEM research. Mission Folder submission. State + regional + national prize tiers. Team prizes up to $9,000 in US Savings Bonds. Schedule: Registration opens August; project submission late February; finals June. Apply at ecybermission.com.

programs.name: Future City Competition (DiscoverE)

cost.display: Free participation; school + non-profit teams welcome

programs.deadline: Project work fall; regional competitions Jan-Feb; finals Feb in DC
programs.description: Annual engineering competition for grades 6-8. Teams design a 'future city' addressing an annual real-world challenge (recent themes: thriving with climate change, future of waste, etc.). Submit a virtual city in SimCity, a 1500-word essay, a 25-square-foot scale model, and a 7-min presentation. Regional winners advance to national finals in DC each February. Free to enter. Strong fit for kids who like systems thinking + creative engineering across multiple disciplines.
programs.scheduleNotes: Free annual engineering competition for grades 6-8. Teams design a 'future city' addressing an annual real-world challenge (recent themes: thriving with climate change, future of waste). Submit virtual city in SimCity, 1500-word essay, 7-min presentation. 39 regional competitions Jan-Feb; finals Feb in DC. Free participation; school + non-profit teams welcome. Schedule: Project work fall (start Aug-Oct); regional comp Jan-Feb 2027 cycle for current school year work; finals Feb 2027 in DC. Apply at futurecity.org.

programs.name: Science Olympiad Division B (middle school)
programs.deadline: Season starts September; regionals Feb-March; nationals May
programs.description: Team-based science competition for grades 6-9 (Division B). Teams of 15 compete in 23 events spanning biology, chemistry, physics, earth science, engineering, and 'study events' (Anatomy, Disease Detectives, etc.) + 'build events' (Air Trajectory, Bridge Building, etc.). Regional → state → national progression. Schools register teams. Strong combination of academic depth + engineering hands-on. Prep starts September; February is when the season heats up.
programs.scheduleNotes: Science Olympiad Division B is the middle school (grades 6-9) tier of the national Science Olympiad competition. Teams of 15 students compete in 23 events spanning all sciences (anatomy, chemistry, ecology, engineering design, forensics, math, physics, etc.). 2026-27 season: school enrolls fall; regional Jan-Feb 2027; state March 2027; nationals May 2027. Team registration ~$60-100; individual events ~$10-20; school + Title I subsidies common. Heavy time commitment (1-2 hrs/wk + intensive prep before competitions) — pairs well with kids who like deep dives + team coordination. soinc.org.

programs.name: American Museum of Natural History Discovery Squad + Children's Camps

cost.display: 1-week day camps ~$575-650; member discount 10%; needs-based aid via AMNH Education

programs.description: AMNH runs week-long age-banded summer camps using the museum's collections + Hayden Planetarium + Discovery Room. Themes vary: paleontology, astrophysics, marine biology, natural history. Kids work with AMNH educators + sometimes scientists. Member registration opens 3 weeks before general — membership pays back via earlier access. East-coast equivalent of Pacific Science Center / Burke Museum camps.
programs.scheduleNotes: AMNH Children's Camps in NYC for grades 1-8 + Discovery Squad for younger learners. Week-long age-banded camps using AMNH's collections + Hayden Planetarium + Discovery Room. Themes: paleontology (Sue + AMNH dinosaur fossils), astrophysics (Hayden show), marine biology, anthropology + cultures. 1-week ~$575-650; member discount 10%; needs-based aid via AMNH Education. Member registration February; general March-April. Camps Mon-Fri 9am-3pm. Find info at amnh.org/learn-teach/youth-and-family-programs.

programs.name: Exploratorium Summer Camps
programs.description: Exploratorium is one of the most influential science museums globally — pioneered the 'hands-on' museum model. Summer camps for ages 8-14 are tinkering- + maker-focused: kids build, take apart, hack, prototype using the museum's exhibits as starting points. Themes rotate (Tinker, Cardboard Engineering, Sound + Music, Light + Color). Bay Area's premier hands-on science camp.
programs.scheduleNotes: The Exploratorium (San Francisco's iconic hands-on science museum on Pier 15) summer camps for grades K-8. Weekly themed camps: Tinkering Studio (engineering + design), Sound (audio physics), Light (optics), Living Systems (biology). Mon-Fri 9am-3pm. ~$525-625/wk; Exploratorium member discount; need-based aid for SF residents. Member reg opens January, general public February-March; sessions sell out spring. exploratorium.edu/education/camps-classes.

programs.name: Field Museum Summer Camps + Junior Curators

cost.display: 1-week ~$425-575; member discount 10%; scholarship via Field Museum Education

programs.description: Field Museum (Chicago, home of Sue the T-Rex) runs age-banded summer camps for grades K-8. Themes span paleontology, ancient civilizations (Egypt, Maya), animal kingdom, ecosystems. Junior Curators track for older kids includes behind-the-scenes lab visits. Strong Midwest equivalent to AMNH / Smithsonian camps.

Member registration January; general February-March.

programs.name: Apple Camp at Apple Store (free)

cost.display: 100% free — including iPad use during sessions

programs.deadline: Sessions July-August; sign up via Apple's Today at Apple in late June
programs.description: Free 90-minute Apple Camp sessions held at every Apple Store nationwide each summer. Topics rotate (animation with Keynote, sketch + animate with Procreate, music with GarageBand, video editing). Kids use Apple devices provided in-store; no purchase or device ownership required. Sessions are usually 3-day series (1 session per day). Sign up at apple.com/today/series. Often the easiest free creative-tech intro for elementary kids.

programs.name: Best Buddies International (school + community chapters)
programs.deadline: Year-round; chapters form at start of school year
programs.description: Best Buddies pairs students with intellectual + developmental disabilities (IDD) with peer 'buddies' for one-to-one friendships, structured activities, and community-building. Middle School Buddies (grades 6-8) + High School Buddies (9-12) operate as school clubs. Pairs build authentic friendships across difference. Strong inclusion + leadership signal — recognized by selective colleges. Schools start chapters via bestbuddies.org.
programs.scheduleNotes: Pairs students with intellectual + developmental disabilities (IDD) with peer 'buddies' for one-to-one friendships, structured activities, community-building. programs.name: Foundation for Jewish Camp — One Happy Camper grant

location.city: 150+ Jewish overnight camps in US + Canada

programs.deadline: OHC grant applications open Nov-Feb for following summer
programs.description: Foundation for Jewish Camp's One Happy Camper grant gives $1,000 to first-time Jewish overnight campers, no income test required. 150+ partner camps span Reform, Conservative, Orthodox, Reconstructionist, Renewal, secular-Jewish, special-needs (Camp Ramah), and culinary themes. Search by camp at jewishcamp.org/find-a-camp. Need-based aid stacks on top of OHC grant.
programs.scheduleNotes: $1,000 grant for first-time Jewish overnight campers — NO income test required. 150+ partner camps span Reform, Conservative, Orthodox, Reconstructionist, Renewal, secular-Jewish, special-needs Jewish camps in US + Canada. programs.name: Catholic Heart Workcamp (CHWC)

programs.deadline: Sessions June-August; book by Feb-March for popular sites
programs.description: Week-long Catholic service mission camps. Teams of teens travel to 60+ host cities (US + a few intl) and serve local communities — home repairs, eldercare, food bank work, ministry. Strong Catholic identity programming (daily Mass, prayer groups) but accepts non-Catholic siblings/friends. 6th graders accepted in some locations (junior camps). Powerful service + spiritual development combo.

Most popular weeks (June + early July) book by February; later July/August often have openings into spring. Adult chaperones required (1:6 ratio).

programs.description: HHF Youth Awards: regional + national recognition for Hispanic high schoolers in 8 categories (STEM, business, healthcare, arts, etc.) with $1,000-$5,000 scholarships. programs.description: Family mindfulness retreats at Plum Village monasteries (France headquarters + 3 US sites). Founded by Thich Nhat Hanh (Vietnamese Buddhist teacher). programs.name: Friends General Conference (FGC) Quaker Family Camp

programs.name: Asian American Journalists Association (AAJA) youth programs

cost.display: FREE for selected; covers travel + lodging for JCamp

programs.deadline: JCamp applications due February for August program
programs.description: AAJA's JCamp is a free 6-day journalism program for ~30 selected high school students from across the US, Canada, and beyond. AAJA covers travel + lodging for accepted students. Note: HS focus, but worth knowing for parents planning ahead from 8th grade.

programs.name: Hispanic Scholarship Fund (HSF) Youth Leadership Institute

cost.display: FREE for selected scholars + scholarship pipeline ($500-$5,000)

location.city: Online + regional summits in major US metros

programs.description: HSF Youth Leadership Institute: pipeline program for Hispanic/Latino youth (grades 7-12) with mentorship, leadership training, college prep workshops, and pathway to HSF scholarships ($500-$5K). Free for selected applicants. Regional summits in NYC, LA, Miami, Houston, Chicago, DC. Online programming year-round. Strong combination of cultural-identity + academic + leadership development.
