programs.name: Sierra Club Inspiring Connections Outdoors (ICO)

cost.display: 100% free for participating youth — Sierra Club volunteers fund all gear + transportation

location.city: 50+ ICO chapters in major US cities

programs.description: Sierra Club ICO connects under-resourced urban youth with the outdoors via free guided trips: hikes, camping, kayaking, snowshoeing, backpacking. Volunteer-led; gear, transport, and food covered by Sierra Club fundraising. 50+ city chapters (Seattle, Bay Area, Chicago, NYC, Atlanta, Miami, etc.). Most chapters partner with schools, BGCA, YMCA, or community centers to reach kids. Excellent low-barrier outdoor entry for kids whose families don't have outdoor gear/experience.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE for participating youth — Sierra Club volunteers fund all gear + transportation. Connects under-resourced urban youth with the outdoors via free guided trips: hikes, camping, kayaking, snowshoeing, backpacking. Volunteer-led; 50+ city chapters. Year-round trips, chapter-coordinated.

programs.name: National Wildlife Federation Eco-Schools USA
programs.description: NWF Eco-Schools USA is the school-based environmental sustainability program — kids audit their school's environmental footprint (energy, water, waste, biodiversity, schoolyard habitat) and lead improvement projects. 7 'pathways' (climate, energy, water, waste, etc.). Schools earn Bronze / Silver / Green Flag certifications. FREE curriculum + tools. International (Eco-Schools active in 70+ countries). Strong fit for kids interested in environmental leadership at school.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE for participating schools (curriculum + certification). School-based environmental sustainability program — kids audit their school's environmental footprint (energy, water, waste, biodiversity, schoolyard habitat) + lead improvement projects. 7 'pathways' (climate, energy, water, biodiversity, etc.). Year-round school enrollment.

programs.name: NPS Every Kid Outdoors (free 4th grade pass)
programs.provider: National Park Service / White House initiative

cost.display: 100% FREE pass — admits 4th grader + 3 adults + all minor siblings to all NPS sites

programs.deadline: Pass valid Sep 1 - Aug 31 of 4th grade year
programs.description: Every Kid Outdoors pass gives ALL US 4th graders FREE entry to all 400+ NPS sites (national parks, monuments, historic sites, recreation areas) PLUS US Forest Service + US Fish & Wildlife sites + US Army Corps lands. Pass admits the 4th grader + 3 adults + all minor siblings in a single vehicle. Get yours at everykidoutdoors.gov by completing a short activity. Valid Sep 1 - Aug 31 of 4th grade year. Easy way to do an entire family of national parks vacations free.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE pass — admits 4th grader + 3 adults + all minor siblings to all 400+ NPS sites + US Forest Service + US Fish & Wildlife sites + US Army Corps lands. Pass valid Sept 1 – Aug 31 of 4th grade year (so the calendar year your kid is in 4th grade Fall semester). Get pass at everykidoutdoors.gov.

programs.name: Audubon for Kids — citizen science + Junior Birder

cost.display: FREE for all youth participation (Audubon Adventures curriculum ~$50 for educators)

programs.deadline: Christmas Bird Count Dec 14 - Jan 5; Great Backyard Bird Count Feb; year-round chapter activities
programs.description: National Audubon Society offers free youth bird-focused citizen science: Christmas Bird Count for Kids, Great Backyard Bird Count (Feb, family-friendly), Junior Birder programs at 500+ local Audubon chapters + nature centers. Audubon Adventures is the K-6 in-school curriculum. Combines real science contribution + outdoor time + photography skills. Excellent low-barrier entry to STEM + environment for elementary kids.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE National Audubon Society youth bird-focused citizen science. Christmas Bird Count for Kids (Dec 14 - Jan 5); Great Backyard Bird Count (4 days mid-Feb, family-friendly); Junior Birder programs at 500+ local Audubon chapters + nature centers. Audubon Adventures classroom curriculum ~$50 for educators; everything else free. Find local chapter at audubon.org/chapters.

programs.name: NOAA Planet Stewards Education Project

cost.display: FREE curriculum + project funding up to $5,000 for educator-led student projects

programs.deadline: Project funding applications due September each year
programs.description: NOAA's Planet Stewards program funds K-12 educator-led student projects on climate, oceans, and weather. Up to $5,000 per project (typical $500-2,500). Free curriculum + monthly virtual seminars. Past projects: schoolyard rain gardens, climate-action campaigns, beach cleanup data, weather stations. Strong fit for kids interested in environmental science with real-world impact + funding to actually do something.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE curriculum + project funding up to $5,000 for educator-led student projects (typical $500-2,500). K-12 climate / oceans / weather. Free monthly virtual seminars. Project funding applications due September each year. Past projects: schoolyard rain gardens, climate-action campaigns, NOAA-data analysis.

programs.name: Outdoor Afro Youth + Family Programs

cost.display: FREE for Outdoor Afro participants — chapter-led trips

programs.description: Outdoor Afro celebrates Black connections + leadership in nature. 60+ city chapters run free hikes, camping trips, paddling, fishing, climbing, and family events. Founded by Rue Mapp. Particularly impactful for Black families historically under-served in outdoor recreation. Chapters in Seattle, Bay Area, Chicago, ATL, NYC, DC, etc. Pairs naturally with NPS Junior Ranger + Sierra Club ICO.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE chapter-led trips. 60+ city chapters run free hikes, camping, paddling, fishing, climbing, family events. Founded by Rue Mapp; celebrates Black connections + leadership in nature. Particularly impactful for Black families historically underrepresented in outdoor recreation. Chapter-coordinated year-round trips. Find a chapter at outdoorafro.com.

programs.name: Earthwatch Kids + Family Expeditions

cost.display: ~$2,000-3,500/wk + airfare; need-based aid via Ignite Awards (covers up to 100%)

location.city: Field sites worldwide (Costa Rica, Iceland, Kenya, Bahamas, etc.)

programs.deadline: Family expeditions year-round; book 6-8 months ahead
programs.description: Earthwatch Family Expeditions: parents + kids join real scientists on conservation field research. 8-12 day trips to field sites worldwide (sea turtles in Costa Rica, lemurs in Madagascar, climate change in Iceland, Caribbean reefs). Kids ages 8+ accepted with parent. Earthwatch's Ignite Awards provide up to 100% scholarships for qualifying low-income youth. Real science contribution + immersive intl experience. Premium pricing but powerful long-term memory.
programs.scheduleNotes: Family Expeditions: parents + kids join real scientists on conservation field research. 8-12 day trips to global field sites — sea turtles Costa Rica, lemurs Madagascar, climate change Iceland, Caribbean reefs Bahamas, mammals Kenya. Kids ages 8-15 with parent. ~$2,000-3,500/wk + airfare. Need-based Ignite Awards cover up to 100% for accepted families. Year-round trips; book 6-8 months ahead. Most family-popular slots run summer.

programs.name: Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools

cost.display: 100% FREE for participating schools (Special Olympics covers all program costs)

programs.description: Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools is the K-12 education program that combines inclusive sports + leadership + whole-school engagement. Three components: (1) Unified Sports — students with and without intellectual disabilities play together, (2) Inclusive Youth Leadership, (3) Whole-School Engagement events. 7,500+ US schools participate. 100% free; Special Olympics provides curriculum, coaching, equipment subsidies. Strongest school-based disability-inclusion program in the US.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% FREE for participating schools. K-12 inclusive sports + leadership + whole-school engagement. Three components: (1) Unified Sports — students with + without intellectual disabilities play together; (2) Inclusive Youth Leadership; (3) Whole-School Engagement. 7,500+ schools nationwide. Year-round school enrollment.

programs.name: Easter Seals Camps + Inclusive Recreation

cost.display: Day camps ~$200-500/wk; residential ~$700-1,200/wk; sliding scale + scholarships heavy

programs.description: Easterseals' 70+ US affiliates run summer camps explicitly designed for kids with disabilities — autism, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, physical disability, sensory processing differences. Programs span day camps, residential weeks, family weekends, and parents' respite weekends. Trained staff with 1:1 to 3:1 ratios. Sliding-scale + need-based scholarships. Some affiliates include 'typically developing' siblings. Find your local affiliate via easterseals.com.
programs.scheduleNotes: 70+ Easterseals affiliates nationwide run summer camps explicitly designed for kids with disabilities — autism, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, physical disability, sensory processing. Day camps ~$200-500/wk; residential ~$700-1,200/wk. Sliding scale + scholarships heavy. Member registration Jan-Feb; general March-April.

programs.name: Camp Korey (chronic illness camp, WA)

cost.display: 100% FREE — including travel + meals + medical care

programs.deadline: Apply 4-6 months before session; sessions disease-specific
programs.description: Camp Korey serves kids with serious medical conditions (cancer, blood disorders, neurological conditions, etc.) FREE including travel, meals, medical care. SeriousFun Network founded by Paul Newman. Disease-specific weeks (e.g., 'cancer week', 'kidney week') so kids share their condition with peers. Full-time medical team on-site. 50-acre site in Carnation WA. Sibling weekends + family retreats also offered. Application via referring physician.
programs.scheduleNotes: Carnation, WA. 100% FREE — including travel, meals, medical care. SeriousFun Network (founded by Paul Newman). Disease-specific weeks (cancer week, blood disorders week, neurological conditions week, etc.). Apply 4-6 months before session. Medical staff on-site. Existing waitlist common — apply early.

programs.name: Friendship Circle (special needs + peer-buddy program)

cost.display: 100% FREE for participating families with special-needs kids

location.city: 100+ chapters in US, Canada, UK, Israel, France, Brazil, Mexico

programs.description: Friendship Circle pairs kids/teens with special needs (autism, IDD, physical disabilities) with typical-peer 'buddies' for weekly home visits + monthly group events + summer programs. Buddies are HS volunteers. 100+ chapters globally. 100% FREE for families with special-needs kids. Founded by Chabad-Lubavitch but open to all faiths/none. Strong disability-inclusion + community for families isolated by their kid's needs.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% FREE. Pairs kids/teens with special needs (autism, IDD, physical disabilities) with typical-peer 'buddies' for weekly home visits + monthly group events + summer programs. Buddies are HS volunteers. 100+ chapters in US, Canada, UK, Israel, France, Brazil, Mexico. Year-round enrollment.

programs.name: AHRC Camps + Recreation
programs.provider: AHRC New York City + AHRC NY State

cost.display: Day camps ~$300-700/wk; residential ~$800-1,200/wk; OPWDD funding covers most for NY residents

location.city: NYC + Westchester + Long Island + upstate NY

programs.description: AHRC New York runs the largest network of disability-focused camps + recreation in NYC metro. Day camps in all 5 boroughs + residential at Camp Anne (NY upstate). For NY residents, OPWDD (Office for People with Developmental Disabilities) waiver funding covers most costs. Open to autism, IDD, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, sensory processing. 1:1 staffing for kids with significant support needs. Sibling Days + family events.
programs.scheduleNotes: AHRC NYC + AHRC NY State day + residential camps for kids + adults with intellectual + developmental disabilities. Multiple sites in NY: Camp Anchor (Long Island), Camp Hunter (Catskills), AHRC's Manhattan day program. Trained staff + therapeutic recreation + adapted programming. Sliding scale; many funded via NY State OPWDD waivers (free for eligible families). 4-8 week sessions Jun-Aug. Apply Jan-Mar for priority. ahrcnyc.org/services/recreation OR ahrcnystate.org. Excellent fit for special-needs kids whose typical day camps don't accommodate.

programs.name: Autism Society Resource Network — local camps + summer programs

cost.display: Varies by local affiliate; Autism Society directory lists state-by-state options + funding

programs.description: Autism Society of America's 75+ state + local affiliates maintain summer-camp directories specifically vetted for autistic kids. Resources include: (a) autism-specific camps (full immersion), (b) inclusive camps (mainstream camps with autism-trained staff), (c) family camps. Most state affiliates also know which Medicaid HCBS waivers can fund camp + respite care in their state. Best starting point for parents new to autism camp landscape.
programs.scheduleNotes: Autism Society's 75+ state + local affiliates maintain summer-camp directories vetted for autistic kids. Resources: (a) autism-specific camps full immersion, (b) inclusive camps mainstream with autism-aware staff, (c) state-funded respite programs, (d) Medicaid waiver-funded options. Affiliate-specific dates + costs. Find your state at autismsociety.org/affiliate-network.

programs.name: American Indian Science & Engineering Society (AISES) Pre-College

cost.display: Most programs FREE for Native youth; AISES National Conference travel scholarships available

location.city: Online + 200+ AISES collegiate chapters + Tribal college network

programs.description: AISES is the leading professional society for Native American/Indigenous people in STEM. Pre-college programs include: Online tutoring + mentorship matching with Native STEM professionals, summer 'Lighting the Pathway' college prep, and access to the AISES National Conference (largest gathering of Indigenous STEM professionals + students annually). Pipeline to AISES college scholarships ($1K-$10K). Open to enrolled tribal members, descendants, and Alaska Natives + Native Hawaiians.
programs.scheduleNotes: AISES Pre-College pipeline for Native American + Alaska Native + Native Hawaiian + Pacific Islander students grades 5-12. FREE annual National Conference (Sep-Oct, varies city). Year-round STEM programming, summer research opportunities for HS, college scholarships ($1,000-$10,000), career mentorship. K-8 students benefit most from AISES Junior Membership ($25/yr — many tribal nations + community orgs cover) which gets them into the conference + Sequoyah Fellowship pipeline. apply at aises.org/students.

programs.name: Native Like Water (Indigenous youth ocean conservation)

cost.display: FREE for accepted Indigenous youth (donations from Patagonia + others fund operations)

location.city: California coast — Pala, Camp Pendleton area + ocean expeditions

programs.description: Native Like Water connects Indigenous youth (Native American, Pacific Islander, Native Hawaiian, Maori, Aboriginal) with ocean + coastal cultural practices. Summer immersion programs include surfing, paddling, free-diving, marine biology, and traditional Indigenous coastal ecological knowledge. 100% free for accepted youth — funded by Patagonia + private donors. Highly selective (~30-40 youth per cohort). One of the strongest cultural-identity + outdoor programs for Indigenous youth in the western US.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE for accepted Indigenous youth (Native American, Pacific Islander, Native Hawaiian, Maori, Aboriginal). California coast — Pala, Camp Pendleton + ocean expeditions. Surfing, paddling, free-diving, marine biology, ancestral ocean practices. Patagonia + other partner-funded operations. Summer programs apply Feb-March. Open to grades 7-8+ (rising HS).

programs.name: Camp Brave Trails (LGBTQ+ youth + family)

cost.display: ~$1,400-1,800/wk; sliding-scale + scholarship pool covers ~50% of campers

programs.description: Camp Brave Trails is the leading summer camp for LGBTQ+ youth ages 12-18. Sessions in California (Angeles National Forest) + Maryland. Affirming community for queer + trans + nonbinary teens with traditional summer-camp activities (hiking, swimming, ropes course, arts) plus identity-supportive programming. Trained queer + trans staff. Sliding scale + scholarship pool covers ~50% of campers. Strong combination of fun + community for kids who may not be out at home.
programs.scheduleNotes: Leading summer camp for LGBTQ+ youth ages 12-18. Sessions in California (Angeles National Forest) + Maryland. Affirming community for queer + trans + nonbinary teens with traditional summer-camp activities (hiking, swimming, arts) + identity-affirming programming. ~$1,400-1,800/wk; sliding-scale + scholarship pool covers ~50% of campers. Book by April.

programs.name: Family Equality Council Family Week

cost.display: Family registration ~$1,200-1,800; scholarship pool covers ~30% of attending families

programs.deadline: Annual gathering early August; register Jan-March
programs.description: Family Equality's Family Week is the largest annual gathering of LGBTQ+ parents + their kids in North America. 1,800+ family members attend each year in Provincetown MA. Programming spans age-banded kids' activities (Tots, Kids, Tweens, Teens), parent workshops, beach time, and community-building. Strong intergenerational queer-family experience — many kids report it as their highlight of the year. Scholarship + travel-grant pools available.
programs.scheduleNotes: Largest annual gathering of LGBTQ+ parents + kids in North America: 1,800+ family members in Provincetown MA. Age-banded kids' activities (Tots, Kids, Tweens, Teens). Family registration ~$1,200-1,800; scholarship pool covers ~30% of attending families. Annual gathering early August; register Jan-March.

programs.name: Interlochen Arts Camp Junior Programs

cost.display: Junior Division (grades 3-6): ~$3,500-5,500/2 weeks; need-based aid covers 30-100% for ~40% of campers

programs.deadline: Apply Nov-Jan; auditions Feb for performing-arts tracks
programs.description: Interlochen is the most prestigious performing-arts summer camp in the US. Junior Division (grades 3-6) + Intermediate Division (7-9) + High School Division. Tracks: classical music, jazz, dance, theatre, creative writing, film, visual arts. Selective (auditions for performing arts; portfolio for visual). Strong need-based financial aid covers up to 100% — about 40% of campers receive aid. Located on a 1,200-acre campus in Northern Michigan.
programs.scheduleNotes: Interlochen Junior Division (grades 3-6) + Intermediate (7-9). Tracks: classical music, jazz, dance, theatre, creative writing, film, visual arts. ~$3,500-5,500/2 weeks. Need-based aid covers 30-100% for ~40% of campers. Apply Nov-Jan; auditions Feb for performing-arts tracks. Estimated typical late June - early August.

programs.name: USA Junior Olympic — multi-sport developmental pipeline
programs.provider: USA Track & Field + USA Swimming + USA Gymnastics + sport-specific NGBs

cost.display: Club registration varies; USATF youth membership ~$30-50/yr; meets ~$15-50 each; many clubs have aid

location.city: Local USATF/USA Swimming/USA Gymnastics clubs nationwide

programs.deadline: Year-round club enrollment; Junior Olympic championships summer
programs.description: Each Olympic-sport National Governing Body (USATF, USA Swimming, USA Gymnastics, USA Wrestling, etc.) operates a Junior Olympic developmental pipeline from local clubs through state, regional, and national championships. Best entry to organized competitive sport for kids beyond rec leagues. Each NGB has its own age divisions, qualifying standards, and scholarship pools. Find local clubs via the NGB website (e.g., usatf.org/youth-clubs).
programs.scheduleNotes: Each Olympic-sport NGB (USATF, USA Swimming, USA Gymnastics, USA Wrestling, etc.) operates a Junior Olympic developmental pipeline from local clubs through state, regional, and national championships. USATF youth membership ~$30-50/yr; meets ~$15-50 each; many clubs have aid. Year-round club enrollment; Junior Olympic championships in summer.

programs.name: Juni Learning 1:1 Online Summer Coding & Math
programs.description: Live 1:1 online coding, math (K-12 through AP Calculus), and STEM mentorship for ages 7-18. Each student paired with a teacher for 50-min weekly sessions; small-group online academies in summertime. 2-week free trial available before paying. Subjects span coding (beginner to advanced CS), math, science, finance, entrepreneurship, communications, test prep.
programs.scholarshipAid: No formal scholarships posted; 2-week free trial allows test-drive before commitment.
programs.howToStart: Visit junilearning.com, schedule a free placement/intro session, then choose subject + cadence.
programs.scheduleNotes: 1:1 online private tutoring for kids ages 7-18 in coding (Python, JavaScript, Java, web dev) + math (Singapore Math, contest math, AMC prep) + reading + writing. Stanford-trained instructors; small program, vetted teachers. ~$300-450/month for weekly 50-min sessions. Year-round + summer; flexible scheduling. Strong fit for families who want consistent personal attention vs group classes. Free trial session. junilearning.com.

programs.name: iCode Summer STEM & Coding Camps (National)

cost.display: Varies by location; full-day summer camps typically $400-$700/wk

programs.description: National network of STEM/coding day camps for ages 6-18 (range varies by location). Themes include game design, drone programming, VEX robotics, 3D printing, Minecraft modding, AI, and YouTube creation. Day camps run 9am-4pm Mon-Fri throughout the summer. 2026 season runs May 26 - Aug 7. Locations include TX, NV, CO, IN, MD, PA, FL, GA, and more.
programs.scholarshipAid: Not posted at corporate level — varies by franchise. Some locations offer multi-week + sibling discounts; ask center directly.
programs.howToStart: Use Find a Location on icodeschool.com, then register through the local franchise.
programs.scheduleNotes: National network of STEM/coding day camps for ages 6-18 (range varies by location). Themes: game design, drone programming, VEX robotics, 3D printing, Minecraft modding, AI, YouTube creation. Day camps Mon-Fri 9am-4pm. ~$400-700/wk full-day, varies by location. Existing deadline Aug 7. Multiple US locations — find at icodeschool.com.

programs.name: Snapology LEGO STEAM Summer Camps (National)

cost.display: Varies by location; typical day-camp week $250-$400

programs.description: Hands-on LEGO + K'NEX + tech STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, Math) day camps for ages 4-14. Year-round programs in schools, community centers, and Snapology Discovery Centers. Themes include robotics, coding, video game design, animation, and architecture. Each franchise independently owned — quality and pricing vary somewhat by location, but national curriculum is consistent.
programs.scholarshipAid: Varies by franchise; some accept Discovery Center memberships that bundle camps.
programs.howToStart: Use snapology.com Locations finder, contact local Discovery Center for camp dates and registration.
programs.dates: Summer schedule varies by location, typically June through August
programs.scheduleNotes: Hands-on LEGO + K'NEX + tech STEAM day camps for ages 4-14. Year-round programs in schools, community centers, Snapology Discovery Centers. Themes: robotics, coding, video game design, magic + engineering, 3D printing. Typical week ~$250-400, varies by location. Existing deadline Aug 15. Snapology Discovery Centers in 70+ US cities — find at snapology.com.

programs.name: Bricks 4 Kidz LEGO Summer Camps (National)

cost.display: Half-day camps typically $200-$300/wk; varies by location

programs.description: LEGO building day camps for ages 5-14 exploring engineering, architecture, robotics, coding, video game design, and stop-motion animation. Half-day options 9am-noon or 1pm-4pm Mon-Fri. New for 2026: 'choose your own adventure' lets each camper pick from hundreds of model plans (motorized models, classic sculptures, mosaics, programmable robots). Every camper takes home a mini-figure and weekly photo collage. Hundreds of franchise locations across US.
programs.scholarshipAid: Not posted at corporate level — many franchises partner with parks & rec departments that subsidize tuition for residents.
programs.howToStart: Find local franchise via bricks4kidz.com Locations, register directly with the franchise or check parks-and-rec catalog.
programs.scheduleNotes: LEGO building day camps for ages 5-14 — engineering, architecture, robotics, coding, video game design, stop-motion. Half-day options 9am-noon or 1pm-4pm Mon-Fri. NEW for 2026: 'choose your own adventure' lets each camper pick a daily LEGO challenge. ~$200-300/wk by location. 200+ franchise locations nationwide; book through local site (find at bricks4kidz.com). Existing deadline Aug 15 covers later sessions; popular early-summer weeks fill spring.

programs.name: Create & Learn Online Summer Coding & STEM Classes

cost.display: Per-class pricing ~$30/hr; free intro classes available

programs.description: Live online small-group (3-5 students) coding, AI, and STEM classes for grades K-12. Featured by Minecraft Education, Code.org, Meta, Roblox Education. Selective instructor pool (<5% of teacher applicants accepted). Free intro classes are a low-friction way to test the format before committing. Subjects include Scratch, Python, AI, web dev, Minecraft, Roblox, Data Science.
programs.scholarshipAid: Free intro classes are de-facto access route. Some bundles + sibling discounts; check site at registration.
programs.howToStart: Sign up at create-learn.us — try a free intro class first, then build a roster from per-class catalog.
programs.scheduleNotes: Live online small-group (3-5 students) coding, AI, STEM classes for grades K-12. Featured by Minecraft Education, Code.org, Meta, Roblox Education. Selective instructor pool (<5% of teacher applicants accepted). Free intro classes are real teaching, not sales pitches — good way to test fit. Per-class ~$30/hr; weekly tracks $80-180. Existing deadline Aug 31. Year-round + summer-intensive; rolling registration at create-learn.us.

programs.name: Codingal Online Summer Coding Camp for Kids & Teens

cost.display: Pricing varies by program length; week-long themed camps + course bundles available

programs.description: Live online coding, AI, and STEM camps for grades K-12 (ages 6-18). Grade-banded curriculum: Scratch + Thunkable for grades 1-3 (block-based, drag-and-drop); web dev, Python, Roblox, Android app dev for grades 4-8; data science, IOI algorithms, and AP CS for grades 9-12. Week-long themed camps include Scratch game-building, Python projects, AI explorations, Roblox studio. STEM.org accredited.
programs.scholarshipAid: Free trial class available; periodic discount campaigns advertised on site.
programs.howToStart: Sign up at codingal.com, take free trial class, then enroll in matching grade-band camp.
programs.scheduleNotes: Live online small-group (1-2-on-1) coding classes for kids ages 6-18. Tracks: Scratch, Python, JavaScript, web dev, AI, ML, Minecraft modding. Indian-origin platform with global reach. Pricing: trial free; ongoing ~$20-30 per 50-min session. 1:1 plans starting ~$50/session. Summer intensive tracks Jun 8 – Aug 31, 2026, 2-4 week packages. Year-round otherwise. codingal.com.

programs.name: NSBE SEEK (Summer Engineering Experience for Kids)

cost.display: Free — fully sponsored by NSBE corporate partners

programs.deadline: Rolling until program start (registration form open spring 2026)
programs.description: NSBE SEEK is a FREE 3-week summer engineering program for students rising into 4th-6th grade (currently completing 3rd, 4th, or 5th). For 2026 the program is virtual-only with rolling admissions. Students complete hands-on engineering challenges with mentorship from NSBE collegiate and professional members. Despite NSBE's name, SEEK is open to ALL students with demonstrated STEM interest — not Black-only. Selection criteria include grade, household income, prior participation, attendance, and NSBE Jr. membership status. Materials kits are shipped to participants at no cost.
programs.scholarshipAid: Program is fully free — no tuition, no fees, materials shipped at no cost to family.
programs.howToStart: Submit the 2026 Virtual NSBE SEEK Parent/Student Registration form via seek.nsbe.org. Apply early — selection is rolling and competitive even though program is free.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE 3-week summer engineering program for students rising 4th-6th grade. For 2026 program is VIRTUAL-ONLY with rolling admissions. Students complete hands-on engineering challenges: building bridges, vehicles, marble runs. Targeted at Black + underrepresented youth but open to all. Materials shipped to home. Existing deadline rolling spring 2026; sessions Jun-Jul. Apply at nsbe.org/program/nsbe-seek.

programs.name: Math Beasts Camp (AoPS Academy / Beast Academy Live)

cost.display: Tuition not posted publicly until spring — typical AoPS summer camps run $400-$900 for 2-4 weeks

programs.description: Math Beasts Camps are AoPS Academy's elementary-tier summer offerings (Camps 2, 3, 4, 5) using the Beast Academy curriculum. Each camp is a 2-week or 4-week live online course meeting 1.5 hours per day, exploring topics not covered in school math (cryptography, game theory, combinatorics) and reviewing/extending grade-level content. Students enter the camp aligned with the grade they will enter (or have completed) in fall, but placement is based on math readiness and can be flexible. Distinct from Beast Academy Online (self-paced curriculum).
programs.scholarshipAid: AoPS offers limited need-based scholarships for AoPS Academy and AoPS Online courses; apply via aopsacademy.org/policies/financial-aid.
programs.howToStart: Create free AoPS account, browse Math Beasts Camp 2-5 by upcoming-fall grade, enroll once 2026 schedule is posted (released in spring 2026).
programs.scheduleNotes: Math Beasts Camp = the K-5 in-person summer + live-online camp version of Beast Academy. AoPS Academy in-person (15 metros) hosts Math Beasts as week-long day camps for grades 1-5; Beast Academy Live runs the online version. Themed weekly camps: Logic + Puzzles, Number Detectives, Geometry Adventures. ~$400-650/wk in-person, ~$200-300/wk online. Mon-Fri 9am-3pm typical for in-person. Year-round Beast Academy continues separately. Apply at beastacademy.com/summer or aopsacademy.org.

programs.name: Northwestern CTD Solstice Online Summer Program (Grades 4-6)
programs.provider: Northwestern University Center for Talent Development (CTD)

cost.display: Tuition varies by course — typical CTD 2-week online courses run ~$1,000-$1,400; financial aid available

programs.description: Northwestern CTD's Solstice Online Summer Program offers advanced enrichment courses for academically-talented rising 4th-6th graders in fast-paced 2-week formats. Courses span math, science, writing, technology, leadership, and service-learning, producing tangible outputs such as writing portfolios, original iOS apps, or community action plans. Admission is by application (test scores or teacher recommendation) — does NOT require district nomination, a common misconception that keeps qualified students out. Distinct from Northwestern's Pre-College HS programs.
programs.scholarshipAid: CTD offers need-based financial aid; eligibility based on family income. Aid applications open with summer registration.
programs.howToStart: Submit eligibility application (test scores or teacher recommendation), review course catalog, apply by spring deadline. No district nomination required.
programs.scheduleNotes: Northwestern CTD Solstice Online Summer for academically-talented rising 4th-6th graders. Fast-paced 2-week course format (online). Topics: math, science, writing, technology, leadership, service-learning. Eligibility: CTD testing OR portfolio. ~$1,000-$1,400 per 2-week course; financial aid via Jack Kent Cooke Foundation partnership. Existing deadline May 15. Specific 2026 weekly slots not surfaced via WebSearch — typical late-June / July / early-August window.

programs.name: CodeWizardsHQ Summer Coding Camps
programs.deadline: Rolling — sessions in June, July, August
programs.description: CodeWizardsHQ runs live online coding camps for ages 8-18, with elementary, middle-school, and high-school tracks. Summer formats: 1-week themed camps (Roblox, Minecraft, AI/Machine Learning, Web Development, Python) plus 3-week accelerated versions of their year-round 12-week core courses. AI Camp covers basics for ages 8-10 and fundamentals for ages 11-13. All classes are live with real instructors (not pre-recorded). 100% money-back guarantee on year-round classes (does NOT apply to summer camps — note before booking).
programs.scholarshipAid: Limited promo discounts (early-bird, multi-camp); no central need-based scholarship program. Multi-pay plans available.
programs.howToStart: Browse 1-week vs 3-week tracks at codewizardshq.com/summer, schedule a free intro consult, enroll. Beginners welcome — no prior coding required.
programs.scheduleNotes: Live online small-group coding camps for grades 1-12 (ages 6-18). Tracks: drag-block (Scratch) → Python + JavaScript → web dev (HTML/CSS) → modding (Minecraft, Roblox). 1-week intensive day camps Mon-Fri ~9-12 + ongoing weekly classes. ~$295-400 per week. Summer 2026 schedule Jun 15 – Aug 21. Smaller cohort sizes than Outschool — typically 4-6 students per teacher. codewizardshq.com.

programs.name: Black Girls CODE Summer Camp 2026

cost.display: Heavily subsidized — most participants pay $0 via sponsorship; nominal materials/transit fee may apply at some sites

location.city: 10 cities (Atlanta, Chicago, Detroit, LA, NYC, Raleigh-Durham, Puerto Rico, plus 3 others) + 2 virtual sessions

programs.description: Black Girls CODE 2026 Summer Camp series 'Game Design: She Won't Just Play the Game. She'll Build It' runs in 10 US cities plus two virtual sessions (Virtual Camp 1: July 7-9; Virtual Camp 2: August 4-6). Girls ages 10-17 (rising 5th-12th) learn game design, build their own games, and develop coding skills using real industry tools to design game assets, narratives, and gameplay mechanics. Includes daily coding instruction, industry speaker sessions, wellness activities, and a capstone showcase. Despite the name, applications are open to all girls with interest in tech (Black girls prioritized in selection but not exclusive).
programs.scholarshipAid: Programs are heavily subsidized — most participants pay $0 thanks to corporate sponsorship. Apply early; selective due to high demand.
programs.howToStart: Apply at wearebgc.org/summer-camp; choose in-person city or virtual session. Sponsorship determines fee tier — most pay nothing. Apply early — competitive.
programs.scheduleNotes: FREE / heavily subsidized — most participants pay $0 via sponsorship; nominal materials/transit fee may apply at some sites. 2026 series 'Game Design: She Won't Just Play the Game. She'll Build It' runs in 10 US cities (Atlanta, Chicago, Detroit, LA, NYC, Raleigh-Durham, Puerto Rico + 3 others) plus 2 virtual sessions: Virtual Camp 1 Jul 7-9, Virtual Camp 2 Aug 4-6. Girls ages 10-17 (rising 5th-12th). Existing deadline Jun 1. Apply at wearebgc.org/summer-camp.

programs.name: AAUW Tech Trek STEM Camp for Girls

cost.display: $50 nominal family fee + transportation; full tuition (~$1,000+) covered by AAUW donations

location.city: University campuses across multiple states (CA, FL, WA, others)

programs.description: AAUW Tech Trek is a week-long residential STEM summer camp for girls entering 8th grade in fall 2026 (rising 8th — currently 7th grade). Campers live in dorms at college campuses, eat in cafeterias, attend STEM labs and workshops, and experience college life. Confirmed 2026 sites include University of San Diego (June 14-20), Sonoma State (June 21-27), Stetson University FL, Florida Atlantic, Pacific Lutheran University WA (July). Tuition is fully sponsored by AAUW donations — families pay only a nominal $50 fee plus transportation to/from campus. Selection is competitive — nomination by school counselor or teacher typical entry path.
programs.scholarshipAid: Fully sponsored — $50 nominal family fee is the only cost, and many AAUW branches waive even that for families in need.
programs.howToStart: Talk to your daughter's 7th-grade math/science teacher about nomination. Then apply through your local AAUW branch — nominations typically due late winter for summer camp.
programs.scheduleNotes: AAUW Tech Trek = FREE 1-week residential summer camp for rising 8th-grade girls (grades 7→8) at 14+ U.S. university campus sites (UC Davis, San Marcos, Whittier, Stanford, etc.). Hands-on STEM curriculum: engineering, computer science, biology, math. Selective application — local AAUW chapters nominate from public middle schools. Apply through your local AAUW branch (find at aauw.org/resources/programs/tech-trek/). Application typically Jan-Mar; sessions run mid-Jun – early Aug. Heavy emphasis on underrepresented + low-income girls.

programs.name: Camp Wonderopolis (Free Online Summer Learning)

cost.display: Free — no fee, no credit card to register

programs.deadline: Rolling enrollment — runs through summer and year-round
programs.description: Free virtual summer-learning destination from the National Center for Families Learning, built around STEM and literacy 'Wonders' boosted by hands-on Maker experiments. Each edition is themed; the current edition is music, with six tracks (Production & Composition, Science & Math, Health, Instruments, Careers, History & Culture). Builds vocabulary, science background knowledge, reading comprehension, and critical thinking. Counselor accounts available for parents, librarians, and after-school staff who want to run a small group. 350,000+ learners worldwide.
programs.scholarshipAid: Not applicable — program is fully free
programs.howToStart: Visit camp.wonderopolis.org, register as a Camper (kid) or Counselor (adult), pick a Wonder track, and start exploring. No download required.
programs.scheduleNotes: 100% FREE — no fee, no credit card to register. Virtual summer-learning destination from National Center for Families Learning. Built around STEM + literacy 'Wonders' boosted by hands-on Maker experiments. Themed editions (current: music, with six tracks). Rolling enrollment year-round. Hidden gem for budget-conscious + homeschool families.

programs.name: Camp CrunchLabs (12-Week Summer Build Box Subscription, Mark Rober)

cost.display: $329.40 for the full 12-week summer program (~$27.45/week); auto-rolls into month-to-month $27.45/month after

location.city: Online + at-home build kits (CrunchLabs HQ: Sunnyvale, CA)

programs.deadline: Rolling — sign up before summer to start with Week 1; weekly boxes ship throughout summer
programs.description: Twelve-week virtual summer engineering camp built around hands-on Build Boxes shipped weekly to your door, paired with exclusive videos hosted by Mark Rober (former NASA engineer / 'Glitter Bomb' YouTuber, 30M+ subscribers). Designed for ages 8-12 (most appropriate for grades 3-7). Each box contains a tinkering project with mechanical, magnetic, or electronic components, plus a video walkthrough and engineering challenges. Each box also enters child into a 'Platinum Ticket' drawing for an in-person trip to CrunchLabs to build with Mark Rober. Standout: combines physical construction with screen-based coaching — rare in the online camp space.
programs.scholarshipAid: No formal scholarship program identified; gift subscriptions sometimes covered by employer-sponsored programs
programs.howToStart: Order Camp CrunchLabs subscription at crunchlabs.com — choose annual prepay ($329.40) or monthly ($29.95) plan, child receives weekly boxes and access to videos. Cancel anytime after week 12 to avoid auto-renewal.
programs.scheduleNotes: 12-week virtual summer engineering camp around hands-on Build Boxes shipped weekly. Mark Rober videos accompany each box. Sign up before summer to start with Week 1; weekly boxes ship throughout. $329.40 for full 12-week ($27.45/wk equivalent); auto-rolls into month-to-month $27.45/mo after. Ages 8-12. Rolling registration.

programs.name: Generation Genius — K-8 Online Science Videos & Lessons

cost.display: 14-day free trial (no credit card); paid family/teacher subscriptions thereafter (price not posted publicly — check site)

programs.deadline: Rolling — free trial available year-round; subscription month-to-month or annual
programs.description: Curriculum-aligned online science platform for K-8 with 117+ video lessons covering 100% of the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). Each video is paired with full lesson plans, hands-on activities, vocabulary, reading materials, and quizzes. Partnered with the National Science Teaching Association (NSTA) and aligned to all U.S. state standards. Videos are self-contained and grade-appropriate — useful for summer enrichment, summer camps, homeschool, or supplementing school curriculum. The 14-day free trial is no-card so safe for parents to test-drive.
programs.scholarshipAid: Title I and underserved-school free access programs available — apply via website 'School Plan' tab
programs.howToStart: Visit generationgenius.com, start the 14-day free trial (no credit card), browse by grade and topic, then convert to family or teacher subscription if continuing.
programs.scheduleNotes: Curriculum-aligned K-8 online science (117+ videos, 100% NGSS coverage). 14-day free trial (no credit card); paid family/teacher subscriptions. Each video paired with full lesson plans, hands-on activities, vocabulary, reading materials, quizzes. Year-round self-paced. Subscription month-to-month or annual.

programs.name: Mystery Science — K-5 Elementary Science (Free Trial Through June 30, 2026)

cost.display: Free trial through June 30, 2026 with access to select units, mini-lessons, and hands-on activities; paid memberships thereafter (price not on public landing page)

Each Mystery starts with an everyday-life question ('Why do leaves change color?') and walks K-5 students through a video story, a hands-on activity using only common household supplies, and a reflection. Strong fit for summer enrichment with parents/caregivers — minimal teacher prep required. Now operates under Discovery Education following acquisition. Summer 2026 curriculum updates are posted on their support site.
programs.scholarshipAid: Free home-edition access historically offered during summer months; check site for current household-account terms
programs.howToStart: Sign up for free trial at mysteryscience.com (no credit card before June 30, 2026), pick grade band, browse Mysteries by topic, queue 1-2 per week as summer enrichment.
programs.scheduleNotes: Open-and-go K-5 elementary science lessons used in 50%+ of US elementary schools. Each Mystery starts with an everyday-life question ('Why do leaves change color?') + video story + hands-on activity. FREE TRIAL extended through June 30, 2026 (select units, mini-lessons, hands-on activities). Paid memberships after trial (price not on public landing page; varies by school vs family plan). Year-round; great summer supplement for science-curious K-5 kids. mysteryscience.com.

programs.name: Maker Camp by Make: (Free Online Summer Maker Program)

cost.display: Free to register and access; physical project supplies vary by activity

programs.deadline: Rolling — 6-week summer session; can be run anytime by family or community group
programs.description: Free 6-week online (and DIY in-person) summer camp from Make: Magazine for kids interested in DIY, making, hacking, electronics, fabrication, and STEAM. 200+ step-by-step project library spanning coding, electronics, fabrication, paper, textiles, music, and more. Projects can be completed solo at home or run as a community group at a library, school, or makerspace — over 2,000 registered Maker Camps worldwide each summer. Badge system rewards completion. All ages welcome; most projects fit ages 7-15 with adult support for younger children.

programs.howToStart: Register a free account at makercamp.make.co (parent or community leader), browse the project library or follow weekly themed adventures, gather supplies, build projects with kids, optionally claim badges.
programs.scheduleNotes: Free 6-week online (and DIY in-person) summer camp from Make: Magazine. 200+ step-by-step project library (coding, electronics, fabrication, paper, textile crafts, STEAM). Free to register; physical project supplies vary. Can be run anytime by family or community group.

programs.name: BrainPOP & BrainPOP Jr. — K-8 Animated Online Learning

cost.display: Family $129/yr (Grades 3-8); +$30/yr or $159/yr combo to add BrainPOP Jr. (K-3); monthly plans ~$30/mo; 30-day free trial

programs.description: Long-running animated online learning platform — Tim and Moby host short topical videos with quizzes, vocabulary, and games for grades 3-8 (BrainPOP) and K-3 (BrainPOP Jr.). Family $129/yr (Grades 3-8); +$30/yr or $159/yr combo to add BrainPOP Jr. Monthly ~$30/mo. 30-day free trial requires CC + auto-converts.

programs.name: Synthesis Teams — Online Problem-Solving Cohort
programs.description: Once-a-week online enrichment cohort grown out of the SpaceX Ad Astra school — kids ages 8-14 collaborate in small teams to solve open-ended, complex problems in 60-minute sessions. Kids ages 8-14 collaborate in small teams to solve open-ended, complex problems in 60-min sessions. Builds creative problem-solving, decision-making under uncertainty. $95/month membership for weekly Teams cohort. Rolling enrollment — join any week. Selective interview/admit (not first-come). Apply at synthesis.com/teams.

programs.name: Steve & Kate's Camp (Bay Area & LA)

programs.description: Steve & Kate's Camp is a long-running multi-activity day camp for kids entering PreK through 7th grade (ages 4–13) with 15+ Bay Area sites (SF Potrero Hill, Cathedral Hill, Emeryville, Fremont, Pleasanton, Walnut Creek, Corte Madera, Petaluma, Santa Rosa, Belmont, Palo Alto, San Mateo, San Jose Berryessa & Willow Glen, Sunnyvale) and multiple LA-area sites (Mar Vista, etc). Day runs 8am–6pm; lunch and snacks included.
programs.duration: Day Pass or Summer Pass; flexible scheduling
programs.dates: Summer 2026 — runs through Bay Area + LA school summer windows

Innovative Day Pass model: $114/day at 15+ pass rate, full Summer Pass available, unused passes auto-refunded — extremely flexible for unpredictable family schedules. Strong fit for kids who get bored with rigid camp structures. steveandkatescamp.com.

programs.name: Lawrence Hall of Science Summer Camps (UC Berkeley)
programs.deadline: Member registration opened late 2025; general public January 2, 2026
programs.description: The Lawrence Hall of Science — UC Berkeley's public science center — runs in-person summer camps for students entering grades 1–6 with hands-on building, experimentation, and discovery-based learning. Distinct 2-week session format (most other Bay Area camps are 1-week) supports deeper content immersion and stronger camper community. Daily 'ammatka Café lunch add-on available. Financial aid application is open for the 2026 season.
programs.scholarshipAid: Yes — Financial Aid application open for 2026 season; submit through Lawrence Hall of Science online portal
programs.howToStart: Apply for membership for early-access registration; otherwise general public sales open Jan 2, 2026. Submit financial aid application concurrently.
programs.scheduleNotes: UC Berkeley's public science center. Distinct 2-week session format (most other camps are 1-week). Hands-on building, experimentation, discovery for grades 1-6. $625-950/wk. Member registration opened late 2025; general public Jan 2, 2026. Financial aid available.

programs.name: CAMP at The Tech Interactive (San Jose)
programs.organization: The Tech Interactive (Tech Museum of Innovation)

cost.display: Member + multi-week discounts available; specific tuition not on landing page — contact The Tech

Brand-new programmatic format (CAMP at The Tech) replacing prior Galileo-at-The-Tech partnership. Cost not posted on landing page — direct booking required.

Member discounts + scholarships.

programs.name: Math Kangaroo USA — International Math Contest (Grades 1-12)

cost.display: $18 standard registration (Sep 15 - Dec 31); $35 late registration (Jan 1 - Feb 1, 2026)

programs.deadline: Late registration closes Feb 1, 2026; contest March 19, 2026
programs.description: International annual math competition founded in France in 1991, now serving 95+ countries and 6+ million students. K-8 students can register through their school or a local Math Kangaroo center; the test is administered the third Thursday in March (March 19, 2026). 75-minute multiple-choice test: 24 questions for grades 1-4, 30 for grade 5+. All participants receive a t-shirt, certificate, and the chance at school/regional/national prizes. Strong addition to a student's intellectual portfolio for high-school admissions and gifted track placements. Local centers can be searched on the Math Kangaroo USA site.
programs.duration: 75-minute test annually + optional year-round prep materials
programs.dates: Test day: March 19, 2026. Registration window: Sep 15, 2025 - Feb 1, 2026.
programs.scholarshipAid: Some local centers offer fee waivers for schools serving low-income students; contact the Math Kangaroo USA office

Top scorers receive medals + certificates; school-team Gold Pin awards. Multi-choice format, 24 problems, 75 min. Apply at mathkangaroo.org.

programs.name: Math Olympiads for Elementary and Middle Schools (MOEMS)
programs.provider: Mathematical Olympiads for Elementary and Middle Schools, Inc.

cost.display: School/team enrollment fee — schools handle registration; check moems.org when 2026-27 enrollment opens in May 2026

programs.description: MOEMS runs five monthly problem-solving contests from November through March for two divisions: Elementary (grades 4-6) and Middle School (grades 6-8). Up to 35 students per team. Schools, homeschool co-ops, or after-school programs enroll the team; individual students cannot enroll directly. Students who score in the top 50% nationally earn awards. Strong precursor to AMC 8/MATHCOUNTS and a measurable elementary gifted-math signal that high schools and admissions consultants recognize. Cost depends on team size; 2026-27 fees not yet posted as of April 2026.

K-8 lines: Kiwi Crate (ages 5-8, science/art/engineering), Atlas Crate (ages 6-11, geography), Doodle Crate (ages 9-16, art/design), and Tinker Crate (ages 9-16, physics/engineering). programs.name: ChessKid.com — Online Chess for Kids (Free + Gold)

cost.display: Free tier (unlimited play); Gold $49/year for lessons, puzzles, computer levels, 800+ videos
